articles.title: New images reveal crater on small asteroid struck by spacecraft in 2022
articles.summary:
Dimorphos, the small asteroid struck by Nasa’s DART spacecraft in 2022 in the first test of a planetary defence system, was left with one side flattened with a stadium-sized crater and is tumbling in space, as shown by images taken by the European Space Agency’s Hera spacecraft released on Wednesday.

DART was sent on a proof-of-principle mission for using a spacecraft to change a celestial object’s trajectory. Dimorphos, an oblong-shaped rocky object about 495 feet (151 metres) wide, orbits its companion asteroid Didymos, with a diameter of 2,395 feet (730 metres), and the pair is currently about 193.5 million km from Earth.

They are defined as near-Earth asteroids, though neither object imperils Earth. Previous data showed how DART succeeded in changing the path of Dimorphos demonstrating that a spacecraft could alter the trajectory of an object headed toward a collision with Earth. Hera is now getting a close-up look at how DART physically changed Dimorphos.

“The side impacted is now completely covered by a crater, with the visual impression that a piece of the asteroid was cut off by the impact. We do not see evidence for major changes on the site opposite to the DART impact.

The combination of those two observations is surprising,” Michael Kueppers, ESA’s Hera mission scientist, said.

The big crater covers nearly the whole front side of Dimorphos as it continues its orbit of Didymos.

“Dimorphos is now tumbling in a chaotic way. There are hundreds of boulders floating around in the system,” Kueppers said. Hera, about the size of a small car, is presently observing Didymos and Dimorphos from a distance of about 25 to 30 km. Hera next month is slated to approach within 13 km of the pair, obtaining increasingly higher-resolution images.

Published in Dawn, November 26th, 2026

articles.title: Gift is not a toll levied at gate of reconciliation: SC
articles.summary:
• Ex-husband ordered to pay Rs500,000 in costs to respondent; LHC order upheld
• Gift deed declared legally ineffective
• Revenue officials told to amend records

ISLAMABAD: The Supreme Court on Wednesday dismissed a decades-old appeal by a husband who claimed ownership of his former wife’s house on the basis of a gift deed, ruling that a property transfer made as the price of reconciliation before the couple’s marriage broke down was not a gift but a “ransom”.

“A gift is a gesture of the heart, not a toll levied at the gate of reconciliation,” observed Justice Shahid Waheed while upholding the 2007 decree of the additional district judge, Lahore, and the Lahore High Court’s (LHC) 2008 decision against Muhammad Iqbal’s pleas.

The Supreme Court bench, which also comprised Justice Naeem Akhtar Afghan, directed the appellant to pay Rs500,000 in costs to the respondent, Sabiha Iqbal, within 30 days of the judgement.

Declaring the respondent the rightful owner of the house and the 1994 “gift deed” produced by the appellant legally ineffective, the apex court directed the relevant sub-registrar and revenue officials to make the necessary amendments to the official records.

“Love gives; coercion extracts. A hiba is born only of the first. What is born of the second is not a gift but a ransom,” the judgement stated.

It said the appeal raised the question of whether a house that a wife was made to sign away as the price of keeping her marriage intact could be considered a gift to her husband. “The answer of Islam, of the statute book and of the conscience of the SC is one and the same: it cannot be called gift,” the judgement explained.

The couple married in 1976 and had two children. In 1983, a six-marla plot in Lahore was purchased in Sabiha Iqbal’s name for Rs42,000. She obtained a loan of Rs81,000 from HBFC in 1985 to construct a house. She maintained that she had also contributed towards its construction by selling her jewellery and receiving financial assistance from relatives. She lived in the house with her children. However, a registered gift deed transferred the property to her husband in 1994. Following their separation in August 1998, she discovered the transfer and filed a suit, alleging that her signatures and thumb impressions had been fraudulently obtained on blank stamp paper under the pretext of arranging loan repayments.

While rejecting the husband’s claim to the property, Justice Waheed also considered whether the appeal should be dismissed without imposing costs. “Given the circumstances stated above, our answer is no,” the judgement said.

The costs, it observed, were not merely the price of losing a case but also served as a balm for the wounds inflicted by a vexatious litigant.

“The respondent has been kept in court for over 28 years over the only home she and her children have. She has been forced to defend, at four tiers of the judicial hierarchy, a title that was hers on the day she bought it,” the judge observed.

“In exercise of our powers under Article 187 of the Constitution, read with Section 35-A of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 and the Rules of this Court, we consider that exemplary costs are warranted, both as compensation to the respondent and as a warning to others who would use the courts to wear down the women they once promised to protect,” it stated.

Published in Dawn, November 26th, 2026

articles.title: PIA passengers in UK left distressed as 2 flights cancelled due to abrupt Norse Atlantic suspension
articles.summary:
Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) said on Wednesday it will move its UK operations to its own Boeing 777 fleet from Nov 26 after wet-lease partner Norse Atlantic Airways abruptly suspended operations, forcing the cancellation of two flights from London and Manchester.

The development came after Norse Atlantic, a long-haul budget carrier, said its financial situation is “critical” and it requires new financing to meet short-term liquidity needs and continue operating.

Hit by soaring fuel costs caused by disruptions linked to the US-Israeli war against Iran, Norse launched a formal process for a potential sale or merger in July and has said it is in talks with airlines about leasing some Boeing 787 aircraft.

In a statement, PIA said flights PK786 from London Heathrow to Islamabad, scheduled for 7:55pm GMT, and PK710 from Manchester to Lahore, scheduled for 7pm GMT, were cancelled.

“Notice of this operational suspension was communicated to PIA without any prior warning just as passengers were preparing to board their respective flights in London and Manchester,” the airline’s spokesperson said.

“PIA shares in the deep frustration and disappointment of every affected traveller and sincerely apologises for the distress, inconvenience, and disruption caused.”

The statement added that to protect passengers from “any further third-party disruptions and safeguard schedule integrity, PIA is transitioning its UK flight operations directly onto its own dedicated Boeing 777 fleet effective tomorrow” (Thursday).

In a later post on X, PIA said its “teams are actively contacting the passengers to re-accommodate on next flights”, referring to those impacted by the two cancellations.

“It is deeply regrettable that our wet-lease partner suspended operations without advance notice at the very moment boarding was set to commence,” PIA stressed in its earlier statement.

It said it was pursuing the matter with Norse Atlantic Airways at the “highest contractual and executive levels”.

On its part, PIA said it took “decisive action to deploy our own aircraft from tomorrow so our customers can travel with complete confidence in PIA’s service continuity”.

Contingencies have already been put in place and PIA’s schedule will operate normally across all network points, the statement affirmed.

“PIA remains profoundly grateful to its passengers for their patience, cooperation, and understanding during this unexpected situation.”

Passengers seeking immediate assistance regarding rebooking or flight schedules were advised to contact PIA’s 24/7 call centre at +92-21-111-786-786, or reach out to its UK station desks at London Heathrow (Terminal 4) and Manchester Airport, or visit www.piac.com.pk.

PIA was privatised in December last year through an auction. A consortium led by Arif Habib Corporation Limited had won the auction for 75 per cent shares of PIA in December last year, making a winning bid of Rs135 billion. The Arif Habib-led consortium had vowed to transform the loss-making airline through operational restructuring, fleet expansion, and improved customer service.

Norse Atlantic says financial situation ‘critical’

In October, PIA signed an ACMI (aircraft, crew, maintenance, and insurance) lease agreement with Norse Atlantic Airways to acquire two state-of-the-art Boeing 787-9 Dreamliners, one of which arrived in Islamabad on Nov 1.

A PIA spokesperson at the time said the addition of the Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner would mark the start of the expansion of the airline’s fleet as it aims to meet rising demand.

Following Norse Atlantic’s announcement on Wednesday about its financial situation, its shares plummeted by 76 per cent at 1:03pm GMT. Most of the airline’s market value has already been wiped out this year.

The Norwegian company is now in talks to secure short-term financing, it said in a statement.

“However, there can be no assurances that such discussions will result in a viable solution,” Norse said.

It did not say how long it could still operate without new financing and did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for further details.

The carrier, which does not hedge its jet fuel needs, cut capacity as costs skyrocketed following the outbreak of the US-Iran war in late February. Many other airlines are faced with the same problem, filing for bankruptcy or initiating restructuring proceedings to survive.

“Long-haul, low-cost is most exposed to high fuel costs as demand is subject to a high level of price elasticity. So maybe not a surprise,” aviation analyst James Halstead told Reuters in response to the Norse announcement.

In a separate development on Wednesday, Norway’s Civil Aviation Authority imposed a fine of 8,000 Norwegian crowns ($814) per business day on the airline, citing its failure to pay financial compensation owed to passengers.

Norse’s plight echoes the wider strain on Europe’s smaller, financially weaker carriers.

Analysts warned during the peak summer season that small airlines could struggle to generate enough cash to get through the winter, with some predicting trouble as early as February, when carriers traditionally run short of funds.

articles.title: Bangladesh ties of 'great importance' to Pakistan, President and PM tell visiting parliament speaker
articles.summary:
Bangladesh Parliament Speaker Hafizuddin Ahmad on Wednesday met with President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in Islamabad, where the Pakistani leaders reaffirmed that Islamabad attached “great importance” to its ties with Dhaka.

The parliament speaker, accompanied by a parliamentary delegation, arrived in the country on Monday on a six-day official visit at the special invitation of National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq. This is the first official visit to Pakistan by a speaker of the Bangladesh parliament, according to the PM Office (PMO).

On Wednesday, Ahmad and his delegation called on President Zardari at Aiwan-i-Sadr, where the president noted that “Pakistan attaches great importance to its relations with Bangladesh, which are rooted in shared history, common faith and deep cultural and familial affinities”, his office said.

The Bangladeshi delegation included MP Jahrat Adib Chowdhury, chairman of the standing committee on foreign affairs; MPs Humam Quader Chowdhury, Muhammad Nazibur Rahman, Nilufar Chowdhury Moni, and Nasser Rahman; as well as Bangladesh High Commissioner to Pakistan Iqbal Hussain Khan.

On Pakistan’s side, the meeting was attended by Sadiq, Senators Sherry Rehman and Saleem Mandviwalla, MNAs Naveed Qamar and Dr Shazia Sobia Aslam Soomro, along with the convener of the Pakistan-Bangladesh Parliamentary Friendship Group in NA.

Later, PM Shehbaz hosted a dinner at the PM House in honour of the visiting speaker and members of the parliamentary delegation.

“Welcoming the speaker and his delegation, the prime minister said that Pakistan attaches great importance to its fraternal ties with Bangladesh,” PMO said.

Recalling the shared history and cultural affinities between the two countries, the premier underscored the importance of closer institutional cooperation and stronger people-to-people contacts.

The prime minister noted that the “extensive engagements of the visiting parliamentary delegation in Pakistan indicate a huge scope of collaboration in parliamentary domain”, PMO said.

He emphasised that regular parliamentary exchanges would provide a robust foundation for closer bilateral cooperation across various avenues of mutual interest.

PMO also shared pictures of PM Shehbaz individually meeting the members of the visiting delegation.

‘Pakistan ready to extend defence cooperation with Bangladesh’

During his meeting with the visiting delegation, President Zardari emphasised the need to strengthen Pakistan-Bangladesh relations through expanded parliamentary exchanges, trade and economic cooperation, educational links and people-to-people contacts, calling for a “forward-looking approach based on sovereign equality, mutual respect and mutual benefit”.

He noted the “renewed momentum in bilateral relations, particularly in high-level exchanges, education, trade, culture and people-to-people contacts”, the Presidency said.

The president expressed hope for the early finalisation of around 26 memorandums of understanding (MoUs) “under consideration, which would provide an institutional framework for expanding bilateral cooperation”.

He “reaffirmed Pakistan’s readiness to extend defence cooperation with Bangladesh”, also highlighting the “considerable potential” for cooperation in agriculture, industry, food security, disaster management, digital governance and space research.

On connectivity, President Zardari welcomed the commencement in January of direct flights by Biman Bangladesh Airlines and emphasised the need to increase flight frequency and destinations in view of growing demand. He also called for exploring direct maritime links to facilitate trade and economic cooperation.

Discussing trade and economic relations, the president noted that bilateral trade remained below its potential.

Therefore, he called for effectively utilising existing mechanisms, including the Joint Economic Commission (JEC) and the Joint Working Group on Trade, to explore preferential trade arrangements and advance the priority areas identified during the JEC session held in October last year.

President Zardari noted that ongoing exports of Pakistani rice under the government-to-government agreement could serve as a basis for broader cooperation on food security and the supply of essential commodities.

“Pakistan, in line with Bangladesh’s request, is also ready to provide technical expertise for the refurbishment of sugar plants in Bangladesh,” the Presidency statement read.

President Zardari encouraged greater private-sector engagement across a range of sectors, including textiles, pharmaceuticals, leather, automobiles, construction materials, minerals, chemicals, ceramics and jute.

He offered Pakistan’s assistance in facilitating training for Bangladeshi parliamentary officials at the Pakistan Institute for Parliamentary Services (PIPS) and sharing its institutional expertise in operating a bicameral legislature.

The president expressed Islamabad’s desire to further strengthen parliamentary cooperation with Dhaka, as well as highlighted bilateral cooperation in the education and media sectors.

President Zardari welcomed progress under the China-Bangladesh-Pakistan Trilateral Mechanism, particularly the identification of 12 priority areas of cooperation during the Kunming meeting on June 19, 2025, the statement said.

He appreciated Bangladesh’s humanitarian gesture of hosting over one million Rohingya refugees, reaffirmed Pakistan’s support for their safe, voluntary and dignified return to Myanmar in accordance with international law, and called upon the international community to ensure sustained humanitarian assistance.

The president expressed confidence that Ahmad’s visit would help advance bilateral relations and pave the way for more high-level exchanges between the two countries.

Meanwhile, Ahmad thanked the president for the warm welcome and hospitality extended to him and his delegation, according to the President House.

The speaker conveyed the greetings of Bangladesh President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.

The statement said: “Recalling his personal memories of Pakistan, he underscored the importance of parliamentary diplomacy and expressed his desire to promote closer engagement between the two Parliaments through exchanges and regular institutional interaction.

“He also noted the popularity of Pakistani television dramas in Bangladesh, reflecting the cultural affinity between the peoples of the two countries.”

Relations between Islamabad and Dhaka have improved since the ouster of former Bangladeshi premier Sheikh Hasina, during whose tenure ties between the two countries remained shaky.

In February, Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal attended the oath-taking ceremony of PM Rahman of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP).

Sadiq travelled to Dhaka in December 2025 for the funeral of the country’s first female prime minister Khaleda Zia. In August that year, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar had also visited Dhaka and met Yunus.

articles.title: KP’s Karak reports 'first polio case in 6 years', taking countrywide 2026 tally to 10
articles.summary:
ISLAMABAD: The National Emergency Operations Centre for Polio Eradication (NEOC) has confirmed the country’s 10th paralytic polio case of the year, with the latest infection from Karak district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

According to an official of the polio programme, the affected child is a 14-month-old girl from the district’s Shnawa Gudi Khel union council.

The case is the first reported from Karak in six years, and the eighth of the year from KP, according to NEOC.

“The case is genetically linked to poliovirus detected in southern KP, where poliovirus circulation has remained intense this year despite an overall transmission reduction in the country,” the official said.

The centre underscored the urgency of consistent vaccination across the country to keep all children protected from lifelong paralysis.

According to the official, Bannu district — which borders Karak — has reported wild poliovirus type 1 (WPV1) in sewage samples for the past eight months, which means that continued virus circulation remains a major risk to children’s wellbeing.

The country’s ninth polio case of the year was reported earlier this month, in KP’s Khyber district. Of the 10 cases reported this year, eight have been reported from KP and two from Sindh.

Pakistan is one of the last two countries in the world, alongside Afghanistan, where polio remains endemic.

Polio has no cure and can cause lifelong paralysis or even death. It is therefore essential that every child under five receives two drops of the oral polio vaccine during each vaccination campaign.

The vaccine is prequalified by the World Health Organisation (WHO) and has been safely used in 195 countries, including all Muslim-majority countries.

With the help of the vaccine and the efforts of hundreds of thousands of polio workers, Pakistan has reduced polio cases by 99.8pc since the launch of its national eradication programme in 1994. The number of cases has fallen from an estimated 20,000 to 31 in 2025.

The third sub-national polio vaccination campaign of 2026, targeting 97 high-risk districts across the country, was launched in October by the Pakistan Polio Eradication Initiative (PEI). The drive was part of intensified efforts to stop poliovirus transmission and protect children from lifelong paralysis.

articles.title: Diesel price dips below Rs350 after 4 months; petrol rate down by Rs4
articles.summary:
The government reduced the price of diesel by Rs5 per litre and that of petrol by Rs4 per litre, according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra).

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs314 per litre and high-speed diesel (HSD) at Rs348 per litre on Nov 26 (Thursday).

The prices of HSD and petrol have gone below the July 18 rate of Rs354.35 and Rs316.15 per litre, respectively.

The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

Under an arrangement announced on Nov 2, for 30 days, oil refineries will contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This allows a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price at the consumer end.

On Sept 17, the government rolled out the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme across the country to ease the public’s burden amid rising fuel prices due to the Middle East situation.

The subsidy scheme applies to owners of motorcycles, rickshaws and vehicles of up to 800cc.

Rise in fuel prices

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50pc for three months.

Since July 17, the government has been revising fuel prices on a near-daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give Ogra the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the conflict. The federal government had also announced targeted relief measures in April to provide subsidised fuel.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

articles.title: At least 3 killed, 14 injured after under-construction building collapses near Karachi's Baloch Colony
articles.summary:
KARACHI: At least three people were killed and 14 injured on Wednesday when an under-construction building collapsed in Karachi Administration Housing Society near Baloch Colony, according to police and rescue services officials.

Rescue 1122 spokesperson Hassaan Ul Haseeb Khan told Dawn that a ground-plus-five-storey building with one penthouse was constructed on 600 square yards and it collapsed when over 20 workers were present at the site.

He added that rescue teams responded immediately, launching an operation with modern equipment and machinery.

He said three bodies and 14 injured persons were recovered from the debris using around one dozen rescue vehicles.

Meanwhile, police surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed confirmed three bodies were brought to Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre (JPMC), adding that another 14 injured were brought to the hospital.

During the initial probe, it emerged that the Sindh Building Control Authority (SBCA) had approved only a ground-plus-one-storey building, East Deputy Commissioner Nasrullah Abbasi told Dawn.

He held that the owner violated the approved plans, adding that when the SBCA ordered construction to halt, the owner approached the court and obtained a stay order against the authority.

Subsequently, the SBCA did not take any further action. He said the building was at the final stage of construction and it had not been ascertained what caused it to collapse.

Meanwhile, East senior superintendent of police (SSP) Zubair Nazir Shaikh told Dawn that three suspects, including a contractor and a family member of the building’s owner, were arrested. He also said the exact cause of the building collapse would be ascertained after proper investigation by the SBCA officials.

Karachi Commissioner Syed Hassan Naqvi told Dawn that the “government will take strict action against those who are responsible”.

Separately, the commissioner’s spokesperson, Sattar Javed, said in a statement that 12 under-construction buildings in different blocks of the Karachi Admin society had been sealed.

Earlier, Sindh Inspector General of Police Javed Alam Odho had directed police officials to reach the incident site immediately and assist in rescue operations, according to a statement from the police spokesperson.

He directed officials to ensure close coordination with Rescue 1122, the fire brigade and other relevant agencies, and take necessary measures to secure the site, remove obstacles to rescue efforts and maintain traffic flow.

Rescue personnel and volunteers search for victims in the rubble of a collapsed under-construction building in Karachi on November 25, 2026. — AFP

The IG also ordered that all available resources be used to rescue people potentially trapped under the rubble and that assistance be provided to ensure the injured receive immediate medical attention.

He directed the traffic police to clear roads, maintain an uninterrupted flow of traffic and make arrangements for alternative routes.

Relevant police officials were also instructed to personally supervise rescue operations and provide regular updates on the situation, the statement said.

Rescue personnel and volunteers search for victims in the rubble of a collapsed under-construction building in Karachi on November 25, 2026. — AFP

SBCA planned to demolish building: Mayor Wahab

Speaking to the media at the site, Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab confirmed that the SBCA had planned to demolish the building.

However, the authority had been unable to do so due to a stay order, he said.

“If there had been no stay order, this building would have been demolished,” he said, underscoring the need to “exercise responsibility”.

“The portion mafia and corrupt elements have caused many losses to this city,” he said.

Wahab also noted that there was “political influence” behind the construction. However, he regretted that when the administration tried to take action, a stay order came from the courts.

The Karachi mayor said that he would discuss the matter with the Sindh chief minister and the local government minister.

“Strict action must be taken to prevent this in future,” he said.

Sindh CM directs SBCA to examine possible negligence, vows strict action

Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah took notice of the incident and directed the relevant authorities to reach the site and expedite rescue operations, said a statement from the Chief Minister House.

He also visited the site to review the ongoing rescue operation, where he was briefed by Local Government Secretary Waseem Shamshad, DC East Nasrullah Abbasi and Rescue 1122 personnel on the progress of rescue efforts and the arrangements for providing medical treatment to the injured.

Speaking to the media, CM Murad said the exact number of people inside the building at the time of the collapse remained unclear due to multiple contractors working at the site.

According to information received from the affected families, around 10 people were reported missing, although rescue officials were still verifying the final number, he added.

Rescue personnel and volunteers search for victims in the rubble of a collapsed under-construction building in Karachi on November 25, 2026. — AFP

According to the chief minister, the building had reportedly been approved for only two floors, including the ground floor, but six floors had been constructed.

Expressing serious concern over the illegal construction, he questioned the role of the SBCA and other relevant departments, stressing that such large-scale violations could not have taken place without the possible involvement or negligence of government officials.

CM Murad said the building owner, consultant, contractor and any government officials found involved would be held accountable for the incident, which he termed not merely an accident but a case of criminal negligence. He vowed that those responsible for the loss of lives would face strict punishment and that justice would be ensured for the affected families.

He warned that negligence by the SBCA or district administration would not be tolerated, adding that officials found responsible would face strict legal action, including imprisonment.

The chief minister also directed authorities to immediately inspect nearby buildings to ensure public safety. He was briefed on the medical facilities being provided to the injured, instructing hospital administrations to remain on high alert and ensure that no negligence occurred in their treatment.

He reaffirmed that the rescue operation remained a priority and that all possible measures would be taken to recover missing persons and bring those responsible for the tragedy to justice.

CM Murad directed the relevant authorities to utilise all available resources to rescue anyone potentially trapped beneath the rubble. He also urged media personnel and citizens to maintain a safe distance so that rescue teams could carry out their operations without obstruction.

In his earlier statement, CM Murad had directed Rescue 1122, the district administration, police and other relevant agencies to coordinate and complete the rescue operation.

He directed the SBCA to examine the building’s approved plans, construction standards and any possible negligence.

The administration was also ordered to determine the cause of the collapse and identify those responsible in case of negligence or illegal construction.

The chief minister also directed the Karachi commissioner and relevant agencies to continuously monitor the rescue operation and submit a detailed report on the building collapse.

President, PM express condolences

President Asif Ali Zardari expressed sorrow at the incident and called for a comprehensive investigation to determine the cause of the building collapse, according to a statement issued by his office.

He added that the investigation should examine construction standards, building plans, and oversight provided by relevant authorities. He directed the Sindh government to take action against those responsible.

President Zardari directed all available resources to be utilised to recover individuals trapped under the rubble and accelerate the rescue operation. He also directed the best possible medical care for the injured.

He further instructed that a safety assessment should be carried out on the surrounding buildings.

“There is no room for any lapse in the discharge of duties by relevant institutions regarding the construction and safety of buildings,” the statement said.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also expressed sorrow at the building collapse and offered condolences to the bereaved family, Radio Pakistan reported.

He directed the authorities to ensure priority medical treatment for the injured, the report added.

Roof and building collapses are common across Pakistan, mainly because of poor safety standards and the use of shoddy construction materials. But Karachi, home to more than 20 million, is especially notorious for poor construction, illegal extensions, ageing infrastructure, overcrowding and lax enforcement of building regulations.

In September, five people were killed and two others injured when a wall of the dilapidated building of a government school collapsed on them in Orangi Town.

Earlier this year, at least 15 people, including women and children, were killed, and 18 others were injured after a gas explosion caused part of a residential building to collapse in Karachi’s Soldier Bazaar area.

In July 2025, at least 27 people died, and 10 others were injured after a five-storey building collapsed in the Lyari area of the metropolis. The building had already been declared uninhabitable by authorities due to its dilapidated structure.

articles.title: AJK Assembly sets conditions for resumption of dialogue with proscribed JAAC
articles.summary:
MUZAFFARABAD: The Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Legislative Assembly on Wednesday offered to reopen negotiations with the proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC), subject to the disbandment of armed groups, surrender of those allegedly involved in serious crimes and an unequivocal commitment to pursue demands through constitutional and democratic means.

The region has witnessed violence-marred protests over the past few months, particularly in June and July, with reports of sporadic unrest in recent weeks. At the root of the tensions was JAAC’s demand to abolish the 12 refugee seats in the AJK Legislative Assembly.

Adopting a resolution unanimously, the House on Wednesday also demanded an end to all sit-ins and illegal protests, reopening of highways and other routes, and a public apology by JAAC’s leadership for what it described as anti-state narratives directed against state institutions, law enforcement personnel, Pakistan and the Kashmir freedom movement.

The resolution, jointly moved by Deputy Speaker Mohammad Ahmed Raza Qadri, Forests Minister Waqar Ahmed Noor, Health Minister Dr Mustafa Bashir Abbasi, Education Minister Umair Naeem, Energy and Water Resources Minister Saqib Majeed Raja and MLA Chaudhry Mohammad Ismail, was read out by Noor. The sitting was presided over by Speaker Chaudhry Tariq Farooq.

The House said the AJK government would be prepared to resume meaningful political dialogue with the committee within the framework of the Interim Constitution of 1974 and relevant laws if the stipulated conditions were met. It maintained that a lasting solution to political disputes lay in constitutional means, the rule of law and mutual respect rather than violence and confrontation.

The resolution held the JAAC leadership primarily responsible for the breakdown of negotiations, claiming that the government had accepted several of its demands and provided assurances on others despite violent protests.

It alleged that JAAC had subsequently interpreted the government’s concessions and flexibility as weakness and raised unconstitutional demands incompatible with the existing constitutional and democratic structure of AJK.

The resolution further said the government had also offered several alternative avenues for resolving the dispute, including high-level negotiations, participation in a multi-party conference and the general elections, seeking the AJK Supreme Court’s opinion on constitutional questions through a reference, and holding a referendum on important constitutional matters.

The JAAC leadership, however, had rejected these options, the resolution claimed.

The assembly expressed grave concern over what it described as attempts to disrupt the timely holding of general elections and create anarchy and uncertainty in the state through armed groups and violent marches since June 2026.

It accused elements affiliated with JAAC of obstructing the movement of law enforcement agencies (LEAs), blocking highways, attacking hospitals, threatening government officials, establishing armed checkpoints and causing the closure of universities, medical colleges, schools and other public institutions.

The resolution also alleged that armed groups had obstructed the supply of essential commodities, opened fire with sophisticated weapons and carried out lethal attacks on law enforcement personnel. It particularly condemned the alleged desecration of the bodies of police personnel martyred during the unrest and restrictions imposed on the movement of ordinary citizens through armed checkpoints.

The House said the violence had severely disrupted normal life, caused shortages of essential commodities and forced women, children and elderly people to leave affected areas for the safety of their lives and property. Access to education and healthcare, freedom of movement and protection of life and property had also been affected, it added.

According to figures placed before the assembly, 34 LEA personnel had been martyred and 248 injured during the unrest, which erupted in June.

The assembly paid tribute to all those martyred and expressed condolences and solidarity with their bereaved families.

At the same time, the House made a distinction between the right to peaceful protest and unlawful activities, reiterating that peaceful demonstrations, political dissent and constitutional rights were fundamental entitlements of citizens, which the state was bound to protect.

It maintained that these rights could not be used as a cover for armed violence, holding citizens hostage, damaging public and private property, blocking highways or attacking state institutions.

The resolution echoed the then-AJK government’s allegations that the JAAC leadership had used social media to promote a narrative contrary to facts and exaggerate casualties, spreading anxiety and speculation among Pakistanis and Kashmiris living abroad.

The resolution warned that in case of non-compliance with its demands, the AJK government should discharge its constitutional responsibilities by taking necessary legal action through LEAs to restore state authority, maintain public order and protect citizens’ lives and property. Such action, it stressed, must remain within the bounds of the Constitution, law and human rights.

The House also paid tribute to the historic contributions of the people of Poonch to the Kashmir freedom movement, expressing the expectation that they would help maintain peace, stability and the rule of law in the region.

Reaffirming its commitment to preserving the existing administrative and constitutional structure of AJK, the assembly said the state’s peaceful, stable and democratic character was essential not only for safeguarding the rights and collective interests of its people but also for the broader objectives of the Kashmir freedom movement.

It resolved that political differences and public demands would be addressed through dialogue and constitutional means, but there would be no compromise on the rule of law, state authority and the protection of public life and property.

Additionally, the House approved three resolutions tabled by treasury members Pir Mazhar Saeed and Sehrish Qamar, as well as Opposition Leader Chaudhry Muhammad Yasin.

Through their respective motions, Saeed called for displaying Quranic verses affirming the finality of prophethood in the Assembly hall, Qamar welcomed the recent visit of the PML-N leadership to Muzaffarabad, and Yasin paid tribute to former president Raja Zulqarnain Khan.

On June 5, following the announcement of the JAAC’s June 9 strike, the then-PPP-led AJK government declared the committee a proscribed organisation and placed it under the First Schedule of the region’s anti-terrorism act (ATA).

A day later, AJK authorities launched a crackdown on the JAAC, arresting scores of its leaders and later placing scores of its activists on the Fourth Schedule of the ATA.

Elections in the region were held in three phases on July 27, Aug 2 and Aug 10 amid protests in some parts. The PML-N — which leads the coalition in the Centre — emerged as the winner.

Earlier this month, AJK President Dr Muhammad Najeeb and Prime Minister Iftikhar Gillani called for restraint and peace, with the latter observing that provocative discourse and prevailing unrest were disrupting the lives of ordinary people.

The remarks came days after the Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) expressed its concern over “reports of a fresh spate of violence in Rawalakot in AJK, with allegations of casualties among both protesters and law enforcement personnel”.

It called for the media to be “given unhindered access to report from the region independently”. “The priority must be to prevent any loss of life and resolve the situation through political dialogue rather than by force,” HRCP stressed.

articles.title: ‘A new era begins’: Pakistan’s Zeeshan Ali becomes first foreigner to board China's Tiangong space station
articles.summary:
Pakistan’s Zeeshan Ali on Wednesday became the first foreign astronaut to board China’s Tiangong space station, marking a historic moment for his country’s science ambitions and Beijing’s efforts to extend its space diplomacy.

The Shenzhou-24 space flight’s three-man crew entered Tiangong at 2:35pm (0635 GMT), roughly six hours after they took off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre in northwest China using a Long March-2F rocket.

The 40-year-old pilot, who is the first Pakistani in orbit, is working as a payload specialist and is set to stay at the station for 5 to 10 days.

To prepare for the flight, Ali trained for seven months in Beijing, during which he underwent intensive Chinese-language classes, learning Chinese songs and reading Chinese poetry. He also practised calligraphy and played table tennis.

The Shenzhou-24 crew, which includes Chinese commander Tang Hongbo and flight engineer Wu Yi, was greeted with hugs by the three Shenzhou-23 flight members currently residing at the station, who had also prepared a cake to celebrate.

“As the first foreign crew member to board the China Space Station, I am incredibly excited. China Space Station here I come!” Ali said in Chinese, according to a report from China’s state broadcaster CCTV.

The two crews then took group pictures of the ninth space get-together in China’s aerospace history. They will now start a new in-orbit handover round, Xinhua reported.

Shenzhou-24 had successfully docked with the Tiangong space station three hours and 38 minutes after liftoff, the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) confirmed.

Chinese broadcaster CGTN said on X that “butter chicken was on the menu” at the space station.

It said that it was hosting “a dinner for six, with a specially curated halal food selection of over 100 varieties for its Pakistani astronaut, including beef nihari, lamb korma and curried chickpeas”.

In the next stage of the mission, Pakistani science payloads will begin in the Wentian and Mengtian labs of the Tiangong space station, according to Suparco’s website for the spaceflight.

Check out more real-time information here.

‘3, 2, 1, liftoff’

A Long March 2-F rocket was used for the launch. It took off in a cloud of flames and smoke at 8:18am Beijing Time (5:18am Pakistan Time) under a pink sky, video from state broadcaster CCTV showed.

A send-off ceremony was also held for three astronauts who make up the mission’s crew at the launch centre before they entered the spacecraft capsule.

The spacecraft successfully separated from the carrier rocket roughly 10 minutes after lift-off and entered orbit, the CMSA said.

“The spacecraft is functioning well. I declare the Shenzhou-24 launch mission a complete success,” an official at the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre announced.

90 experiments

China’s Tang Hongbo is commanding the mission, with Wu Yi serving as mission pilot and Ali as payload specialist.

Ali is expected to spend around a week in space, conducting various experiments alongside the Chinese crew. Pakistan’s space agency, Suparco, said Ali would conduct experiments in orbit, including cultivating microalgae as a potential food and oxygen source for future space missions, and testing the effects of spaceflight on quinoa seeds.

Meanwhile, the CMSA said the crew would conduct around 90 experiments during the mission.

The agency said the mission’s objectives included conducting an orbital rotation with the crew of the earlier Shenzhou-23 mission, carrying out routine operations and maintenance of the space station, and continuing space science research, including experiments involving space payloads.

‘Pakistan begins its journey beyond the stars’

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif congratulated the nation on astronaut Zeeshan Ali’s departure for the Tiangong space station aboard China’s Shenzhou-24 mission, saying Pakistan had begun its journey “beyond the stars”, the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said.

In a statement, the prime minister said the “journey was not just that of one astronaut but of 240 million Pakistanis, particularly the younger generation, scientists and their dreams”.

He said Zeeshan Ali and Khurram Daud had completed their training in China with hard work, discipline and dedication.

Shehbaz said Pakistan would become the first country after China to travel to the Tiangong space station, calling the development a reflection of the “ironclad friendship” between the two countries.

He thanked China for making Pakistan part of the historic mission, adding that the two countries were now working together not only for peace and development on Earth but also in space.

The prime minister also paid tribute to Suparco, universities and scientists involved in the scientific experiments being sent into space.

The premier said the combined efforts of the armed forces, national institutions, scientists and young people were helping Pakistan make progress in space research and advanced science.

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar also congratulated the people of Pakistan and China on the successful launch of Shenzhou-24.

“This historic mission marks a significant milestone in our all-weather strategic cooperative partnership as we commemorate 75 years of diplomatic relations.”

“I thank President Xi Jinping and the Chinese leadership for their support and commend the teams of both countries for this achievement, which reflects our enduring friendship and commitment to the peaceful exploration of space,” he posted on X.

Dar said it was a “proud moment” for Pakistan, and this mission would inspire the country’s youth and advance its aspirations in science and technology.

“My best wishes to our astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali and the Chinese crew for a safe journey and a successful mission,” he concluded.

The military leadership has congratulated the nation, the Suparco and the scientific community on the historic launch of Pakistan’s first astronaut to China’s Tiangong space station, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said in a press release.

Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, Chief of the Naval Staff Admiral Naveed Ashraf, Chief of the Air Staff Air Chief Marshal Zaheer Ahmed Baber Sidhu, and Commander National Strategic Command General Syed Aamer Raza extended felicitations on behalf of the Armed Forces of Pakistan.

The ISPR said the journey of Zeeshan Ali, Pakistan’s first astronaut and the first foreign astronaut to travel to the Chinese space station, marked a defining moment in the country’s scientific and technological advancement and was a source of immense pride for the nation.

The military leadership commended Suparco’s scientists, engineers and technical teams for their dedication, professionalism and sustained efforts in achieving the milestone.

It also appreciated the leadership, government and people of China for their support and cooperation in enabling Pakistan to achieve the milestone.

The ISPR said the friendship between Pakistan and China had reached new heights, extending beyond the frontiers of Earth into outer space.

It added that Pakistan’s entry into human spaceflight reflected the potential of its human capital, scientific ingenuity and technological capabilities, and would inspire future generations to pursue excellence in science, technology and innovation.

The armed forces also wished Zeeshan Ali success and a safe return to Earth.

Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal, who is in China, witnessed the send-off and the mission’s launch.

Later, he posted on X: “As Shenzhou-24 lifts off this morning, Nov 25, carrying Zeeshan Ali, Pakistan’s first astronaut, a new era begins for Pakistan’s space programme. With him, the Pakistani flag rises into orbit, lifting the hopes and aspirations of 260 million Pakistanis for technological advancement and space exploration. From highways to information super highways to skyways, Pakistan-China friendship and CPEC rises higher than the skies.

“This is Pakistan’s URAAN (flight) into space, and it is only the beginning of a brighter and more glorious future.”

Zardari, Xi exchange letters

Meanwhile, the Presidency in Islamabad said in a statement that President Asif Ali Zardari had exchanged letters with his Chinese counterpart on the “landmark Pakistan-China space cooperation achievement”.

The statement said the two leaders congratulated each other on the “historic milestone in Pakistan-China space cooperation, marked by the first spaceflight of a Pakistani astronaut to China’s space station aboard the Shenzhou spacecraft, making him the first foreign astronaut to enter the Chinese space station”.

President Zardari extended felicitations to the government and people of China and expressed his “profound appreciation” for selecting Pakistan as the first foreign partner in China’s manned space programme, the statement said. It added that he further acknowledged the “invaluable support, professionalism and dedication” of the CMSA and the Astronaut Centre of China in making the collaboration possible.

President Zardari said the achievement “reflects China’s remarkable progress in space science and technology as well as its commitment to international cooperation in the peaceful exploration and use of outer space”.

He said the initiative embodied the “vision of building a community with a shared future for mankind, based on mutual progress, shared opportunities and collective advancement”.

He further wrote: “Pakistan takes immense pride in this historic achievement, which stands as another testament to the enduring friendship, mutual trust and close cooperation between the two countries.”

The president noted that collaboration between CMSA and Suparco had opened new avenues for bilateral cooperation in science, technology and space exploration.

He expressed confidence that the “achievement would inspire generations of young Pakistanis to pursue excellence in scientific research, innovation and technological advancement”.

In his letter, President Xi congratulated the government and people of Pakistan, the astronauts of both countries and their teams in the space industry.

President Xi said the astronauts from both countries “joining hands in the quest for the universe represents a living testament to their deep-rooted friendship and a new and significant outcome of bilateral cooperation”.

He noted that exploration was never-ending as the cosmos is boundless.

“The Chinese space station is an ark of peace, friendship and cooperation. China, together with [other] countries, including Pakistan, stands ready to hold high the banner of peaceful uses of outer space, deepen international space cooperation and improve global outer space governance, to ensure that outer space exploration delivers greater benefits to the humanity,” he added.

‘Carrying hopes of 250m Pakistanis’

In April, Zeeshan Ali and Khurram Daud were chosen from Pakistan to start training in China. Pakistan’s space agency Suparco and CMSA signed a cooperation agreement in February 2025, under which two Pakistanis were to train in China, with one joining a mission on the Tiangong space station operated by Beijing.

Eventually, Ali was chosen to join the Chinese mission.

Speaking at a press briefing in Jiayuguan on Tuesday, Ali said he was “deeply grateful” to the Chinese government for helping “us realise our dream of going into space”.

He said he arrived at the Astronaut Centre of China a few months ago, carrying with him the hopes of 250 million Pakistani people.

Ali said he believed that “what comes after this flight matters more than the flight itself”.

“This mission is not a finish line; it is a launch pad. And I hope the next chapter of China-Pakistan space cooperation will grow from one astronaut, one flight to multiple joint flights, to the Moon, Mars and beyond.”

Addressing Pakistanis, he said: “I now feel the true weight of the words of our Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, when he told me that we were about to write a new chapter in Pakistan’s history. I want to assure you that I am not flying for myself. I carry the name of Pakistan on my shoulders, the hopes of 250 million Pakistanis.

“To every child who is watching while I am in orbit, just look up at the sky and remember that I am up there with your dreams.”

In his message to his family, he said: “I want to say that I will travel farther from home than ever before. But I promise you one thing: whenever I look back at the Earth for the first time, I will always search for the light of our home before I look at anything else. No matter how far I fly, we will still share the same Moon, and I will still be looking back at the same Earth.”

Stay at Tiangong

China’s self-built station, named Tiangong or Celestial Palace in Chinese, has been fully operational since late 2022. It can host up to six astronauts during handovers when an arriving three-person crew overlaps with the departing crew.

This time, the handover will be different.

Shenzhou-23 commander Zhu Yangzhu ​will stay on to support Beijing’s study ​of how the human body copes ⁠in space — a crucial step towards a planned crewed mission to the moon and a potential journey to Mars. The rest of the Shenzhou-23 crew will depart Tiangong alongside Ali.

Zhu, who will stay for a year, will hold the record for the longest single ​stay in orbit by a Chinese astronaut by the time he leaves.

Beijing has poured billions into China’s space programme as it aims to land astronauts on the Moon before 2030, a race in which the United States is also competing with its Artemis programme.

Additional input from AFP

articles.title: Trump says he will meet 'smart guy' Abdul El-Sayed on universal healthcare
articles.summary:
United States President Donald Trump said on Tuesday he would meet with Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed to discuss universal healthcare, signalling a possible opening for cooperation after a combative election campaign.

“I know I’ll be meeting with him,” Trump told the New York Post in an Oval Office interview, referring to El-Sayed’s proposal to rebrand Medicare for All as “Trumpcare”.

“Maybe there’s some place in the middle that we could go,” Trump added, suggesting room for compromise on healthcare reform.

Trump described El-Sayed as “a smart guy” and said he had done “a very good job” promoting the idea.

El-Sayed made universal healthcare a central issue in his campaign and sought to appeal directly to Trump by proposing that the plan carry the president’s name.

Earlier this month, El-Sayed posted an image of a gold “Trumpcare” card on US social media company X, urging the president to guarantee healthcare coverage “from cradle to grave”.

Trump called the branding idea “very smart” and said he saw room to work with the incoming Democratic majorities in Congress, though he expected tensions at first.

“I’m just going to veto everything there is, and then at some point I think they’re going to want to negotiate,” he said. “I will, and we can do health care. We can do a lot of great things together.”

Trump repeatedly attacked El-Sayed during the campaign, while the Michigan Democrat was a vocal critic of the Trump administration. El-Sayed is set to become the first Muslim US senator.

Republicans ran a scorched-earth campaign to paint Democrats as communists and branded El-Sayed a terrorist who would endanger Americans.

But the straight-talking 42-year-old El-Sayed pledged to help cash-strapped voters navigate America’s fractured, for-profit health care system.

During the race, El-Sayed drew huge campaign crowds across the state, even in deeply conservative Republican areas.

El-Sayed also vowed to get “money out of politics” and address the harsh economic woes that have voters yearning for a political newcomer to shake up the status quo.

articles.title: India says 'cockroach' movement leader Das told not to use passport
articles.summary:
India’s foreign ministry said on Wednesday that passport authorities asked ‘cockroach’ movement leader Saurav Das not to ​use his passport until he clarified information about ‌his place of birth.

On Monday, Das said he was stopped at Delhi airport hours before he was due to fly to London ​to speak to students, after being issued the passport ​notice. Das accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government of ⁠trying to silence dissent and stifle debate by blocking ​his travel to Britain.

Indian foreign ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said ​passport authorities issued a notice if a discrepancy was noted or reported, amounting to a suppression of facts.

“He was also advised not to ​use the passport until he had submitted his response,” ​Jaiswal told a regular media briefing, referring to Das.

Das has petitioned the ‌Delhi ⁠High Court against the government move, legal news website LiveLaw reported. The plea will be heard on Thursday.

Das was among 14 people who scaled barricades on October 13 to enter ​the Jantar Mantar ​observatory in ⁠central Delhi, a day after it was removed from a list of designated protest sites. ​He was detained for a few days. He led ​thousands ⁠of youth supporters demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation over voter list revisions that critics say favour Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party.

This ⁠followed ​a weeks-long sit-in by supporters of the ‘cockroach’ ​movement earlier this year that forced Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan to resign over ​exam paper leaks.

articles.title: NCCIA claims busted call centre at Karachi's Sharea Faisal defrauding elderly US citizens
articles.summary:
The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) said on Wednesday that it had busted a call centre in Karachi for fraud, arresting five people and recovering Rs150 million in cash as well as about Rs60m in cryptocurrency.

According to a press release issued by the agency, the call centre allegedly defrauded elderly United States citizens with claims surrounding medical equipment and health insurance.

The network allegedly operated under the names ‘Global Resource Group’, ‘Phoenix Marketing Solution’ and ‘The Call Solution’ between 2020 and 2025 from offices at Anam Empire on Sharea Faisal, the NCCIA alleged.

It added that the network moved about Rs1.2bn to Pakistan in “proceeds of crime”.

A first information report (FIR) was registered against 10 suspects, the statement said, adding that five had been arrested. The other five, including a bank branch manager, were absconding and efforts to recover them were underway.

The FIR invoked Sections 3 (unauthorised access to information system or data), 4 (unauthorised copying or transmission of data), 13 (electronic forgery), 14 (electronic fraud), 16 (unauthorised use of identity information) and 26 (spoofing) of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca), read with sections 34 (common intention) and 109 (abetment) of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC).

The probe was also widened to cover money laundering under the Anti-Money Laundering Act, 2010. The agency said the assets bought with the money were currently being identified, along with other accomplices and cross-border facilitators.

“According to the investigation, the accused made unsolicited calls to elderly patients in the United States. They misrepresented the eligibility, coverage and insurance benefits of durable medical equipment (DME) products”, which gave them access to the personal and medical information of their victims, the NCCIA said.

It added that the data was passed to a US-based medical billing partner, which submitted unlawful claims to US health insurers including Medicare, Humana and UnitedHealthcare. The billing partner kept “its commission and expenses” while the rest of the money was shared among the suspects.

The money was brought to Pakistan through “illegal hawala/hundi channels and merchant facilities” and received in cash and through dummy bank accounts belonging to fictitious companies and firms, the NCCIA said, noting that 23 such accounts had been identified.

“Approximately Rs1.2bn was debited and credited through these accounts in a short period,” it said.

“The money was then allegedly spent on movable and immovable property and digital assets to hide its illegal origin.”

Rs150m in cash was recovered, alongside a currency-counting machine, four luxury vehicles estimated to cost Rs48m, about Rs60m in cryptocurrency identified in a Binance account, and digital evidence including 11 mobile phones, tablets and laptops; a passport and bank records of the fictitious firms.

Earlier this month, the NCCIA claimed to have conducted a major operation against an alleged international fraud network and arrested 273 people from a call centre located on Sharea Faisal. In a separate raid in October, it claimed to have arrested over 40 suspects in a raid on another “illegal call centre” located on the same road.

In September, more than 70 people were arrested in two raids on as many call centres in PECHS for allegedly targeting US citizens through fraudulent schemes involving offers for new credit cards and low-interest financial services.

articles.title: Tarar urges social media companies to establish offices in Pakistan
articles.summary:
Federal Information Minister Attaullah Tarar on Wednesday urged social media companies to establish their offices in Pakistan and expand their presence in the country.

He made the remarks while addressing a seminar organised by the Sustainable Policy Development Institute in Islamabad.

“Social media platforms are most welcome. We want their business to grow in Pakistan,” he said.

The minister said that the country needed their presence as it had a vibrant youth population that created “positive content”.

“We have the potential to create good and positive content and these social media companies can benefit from that content.

“They should open their offices in Pakistan,” Tarar urged.

At the same time, the minister said that social media was “financially incentivising terrorism, harassment against women and child abuse”.

“Anything that goes viral is directly linked to financial incentives. Social media platforms are paying you according to your [number of] views,” he said.

“There is an algorithmic injustice,” he declared.

“Social media has failed to protect the dignity and privacy of citizens,” the minister went on to say.

He said that the government had been engaging with the social media platforms on various matters. However, the government could not push social media companies to adhere to the laws of the country, Tarar said.

He said that whenever the government spoke to these companies, they said that they were very eager to open their offices in Pakistan and enhance their presence.

“We are ready to work with all social media platforms to help them formulate their policy according to local peculiarities,” he maintained. Tarar argued that it could not be a one-size-fits-all fix as every country had its own dynamics and issues.

The remarks come a day after Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi asserted that freedom of speech should not become a shield for those who cross “red lines”, adding that terrorism, hate speech, incitement to violence and sexual exploitation of children were the four non-negotiable red lines for the state.

“This is not about technology; this is about people. We are not saying that free speech must be curtailed. Journalists must report, citizens must question and dissent must be heard, including criticism of the government. But freedom of speech can never become a shield for those who cross these red lines,” the interior minister said.

articles.title: US unveils proposed tariffs on major partners, including EU, China and India
articles.summary:
The United States on Wednesday unveiled proposed tariffs on 14 economies, including the European Union, China and India, after a months-long probe into alleged excess production — the latest move by US President Donald Trump to remake Washington’s trade relationships.

The duties, proposed at up to 20 per cent, come over allegations that the economies “are promoting production and capacity divorced from the realities of demand and market principles,” a senior US official said on condition of anonymity.

The new tariffs will need to undergo a period of public comment before taking effect, with the official adding that the proposals take existing trade deals into account.

The new levies target some of the United States’ largest trading partners, including China, the European Union, India, Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Singapore, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand and Vietnam.

The US official made specific mention of China, for whom a 20pc tariff is being proposed, the joint-highest for any economy.

In a separate announcement, the US Trade Representative’s office also proposed additional tariffs on goods from Brazil, including aircraft, over alleged inaction on addressing US trade concerns.

Trump’s tariffs have targeted Washington’s friends and foes alike, and are part of a push in his second term to remake global trade by forcing countries to buy US products or produce their goods in his country.

The latest move offers some relief for partners that earlier signed tariff deals with the Trump administration, but it could still raise temperatures as the US president prepares to host G20 leaders in Miami in December.

“We don’t expect this to create tension or rancor” at the G20 summit, the senior US official said. “We actually expect that we may be signing more agreements at the G20 in the wake of these announcements.”

Inflation pressures

Over-capacity concerns affect a range of sectors, from batteries to cement, chemicals to processed food, the senior US official said.

The duties could add further pressure on US businesses already squeezed by earlier tariffs, with firms now likelier to pass on costs to consumers already frustrated with the high cost of living.

Affordability was a key issue in recent midterm elections, which saw Trump’s Republican Party swept out of power in both houses of Congress by Democrats.

US consumer inflation came in at 3.7pc year-on-year in September, close to a three-year high as prices are pushed up by the effects of Trump’s war on Iran, tariffs, and the massive AI investment boom.

US Federal Reserve policymakers, responsible for keeping inflation to a long-term two-per cent target, say that most price effects of Trump’s previous tariff rollout have passed through the economy — but any new levies could push prices up further.

The new tariffs are likely to come into effect in January at the earliest, the senior US official said.

Trump’s latest duties come after an investigation the US Trade Representative started in March on excess manufacturing capacity and production.

The concern was whether other countries were taking actions deemed “unreasonable or discriminatory,” and if they weighed on US commerce.

The probes came days after the US Supreme Court struck down Trump’s previous slew of tariffs, holding that the president did not hold the authority to impose the duties using the law the White House had cited.

Pushback expected

Trade lawyer Ryan Majerus told AFP that he expected this probe to be among “the most important” actions for the Trump administration, given its underlying concern that factories with excess capacity start operations abroad and “never get turned off, even if there’s no demand.”

This potentially leads to an oversupply of goods, depressed prices and a “hollowing out” of US manufacturing, he added.

The US determination is likely to face strong pushback from China and others, with Beijing long rejecting criticism that it relies too much on exports to boost its economy.

While the US Supreme Court struck down Trump’s global tariffs in February, his sector-specific duties remain intact.

The new tariffs will not stack on top of those sector-specific tariffs on items like automobiles and steel, the senior US official said.

In July, Trump imposed a separate wave of tariffs on 60 economies, accusing them of insufficient action against forced labour.

For economies facing both the forced labour and excess production tariffs, the levies would not stack, the US official said. Instead, the higher rate of the two would prevail.

articles.title: £190m corruption case: Imran, Bushra's counsel says transaction caused no loss to exchequer
articles.summary:
ISLAMABAD: In the £190 million corruption case, counsel for PTI founder and former prime minister Imran Khan and his wife, Bushra Bibi, argued that the transaction had caused no loss to the national exchequer but had instead proved financially beneficial.

The couple is serving prison sentences in the £190 million corruption case, also known as the Al-Qadir Trust case. On January 17, 2025, an accountability court in Islamabad sentenced Imran to 14 years in prison and Bushra to seven years in the case. Both subsequently challenged their convictions before the IHC.

The development came as the Islamabad High Court (IHC) resumed hearing appeals filed by Imran and Bushra against their convictions on Wednesday.

A division bench comprising IHC Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar and Justice Muhammad Asif heard the appeals.

At the outset, Barrister Salman Safdar, counsel for the appellants, sought live streaming of the proceedings, arguing that the facility was available in courts across Pakistan and in other countries.

He said the request was aimed at ensuring transparency in a case involving matters of public importance. The counsel clarified that he was not seeking a telecast of the proceedings on Pakistan Television but wanted them to be live-streamed for public access.

Barrister Safdar pointed out that the trial had been conducted behind closed doors inside Adiala jail, arguing that open, live-streamed proceedings before the IHC would help address the lack of public access during the trial.

Justice Dogar observed that arguments concerning the May 9 incident and other general matters were irrelevant to the proceedings. He advised the counsel to focus on the pending application and the legal issues involved in the appeals.

Justice Dogar also pointed out that the IHC proceedings were already open to the public and that the courtroom was crowded.

When Barrister Safdar mentioned that Imran was 74 years old and incarcerated, the chief justice advised him to advance legal arguments rather than refer to general information about the appellant.

The counsel cited the case of former military ruler General (retd) Pervez Musharraf and read excerpts from Indian court judgments in support of his plea for live-streaming.

However, Justice Dogar observed that rules governing live-streaming were yet to be finalised and that the application could not be allowed at this stage.

Barrister Safdar requested the court to adjourn the application until the rules were framed, expressing hope that the matter would be resolved soon. He said that, as an advocate, he considered it appropriate to advance legal arguments even if the judge was initially reluctant to accept his request.

The chief justice observed that the conduct of proceedings was at the court’s discretion.

Arguing the main appeals, Barrister Safdar said the prosecution had produced 35 witnesses during the trial and Imran had been convicted under various provisions of the National Accountability Ordinance.

He elaborated that Imran was formally arrested in the case on November 13, 2023, while Bushra was convicted of abetment and arrested after her conviction.

The counsel pointed out that several individuals, including former accountability adviser Mirza Shahzad Akbar, property tycoon Malik Riaz, his son Ahmed Ali Riaz, Zulfikar Bukhari, Farhat Shahzadi and Ziaul Mustafa Nasim, had been declared absconders in the case.

Reading from the charge sheet, he said Akbar had produced a letter from the UK’s National Crime Agency (NCA) regarding the freezing of accounts belonging to Riaz and his family members.

He said the accounts had been frozen in three phases and maintained that the alleged financial benefits to Imran and Bushra had been extended before the accounts were frozen.

He also referred to the prosecution’s allegation that Bahria Town had extended financial benefits to Imran and Bushra through Bukhari in April 2019 under the guise of donations.

However, he pointed out that Riaz’s money had been frozen on August 12, 2019. Initially, the allegation against Imran was one of abetment, but Imran was subsequently made the principal accused, the counsel added.

According to the prosecution’s case, Imran allegedly approved the transfer of the frozen funds to an account maintained by the Supreme Court in violation of the Rules of Business. The funds were linked to Rs460 billion that Riaz was supposed to deposit in connection with the Bahria Town land dispute in Karachi.

Barrister Safdar argued that the amount had been transferred to the SC account even before the Federal Cabinet’s approval.

He alleged that Akbar and Nasim, both absconders in the case, had played a role in placing the relevant summary before the cabinet and facilitating the transfer.

The counsel further added that the prosecution’s case was that the amount should have been deposited with the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) rather than the apex court account to settle a civil liability.

Referring to the Al-Qadir University land transaction, he said the land had been transferred in January 2021. The prosecution had alleged that Riaz provided Rs285 million for the university’s building and furniture, but the amount was never transferred to Imran or Bushra’s personal accounts, the counsel argued.

The counsel said Imran was accused of chairing a cabinet meeting on December 3, 2019, and misleading its members into approving the transfer to benefit Riaz.

He maintained that the funds were deposited in the SC account and subsequently invested in profitable ventures, generating substantial returns.

“The amount remained with the Supreme Court for four years, and everyone knew about it,” he argued, adding that the funds had yielded significant profits.

Barrister Safdar further argued that Akbar had held multiple positions, including special assistant to the prime minister, chairman of the Assets Recovery Unit and adviser on accountability. He alleged that Akbar, in connivance with others, had played a key role in signing the confidentiality agreement that paved the way for the recovery of the frozen funds.

He contended that there was no evidence establishing Imran’s active knowledge of any alleged wrongdoing and that neither Imran nor Bushra had signed the confidentiality agreement.

He also questioned how Imran could have been aware of any alleged irregularities when the National Accountability Bureau (NAB) itself was part of the Assets Recovery Unit.

When Justice Dogar observed that the Assets Recovery Unit was an independent entity, Barrister Safdar responded that it comprised officials from NAB, the Federal Investigation Agency and SBP.

“If these officials were unaware of any wrongdoing, how could Imran Khan have known about it?” he questioned.

The counsel argued that the transaction did not cause any loss to the national exchequer, as the amount had remained within the banking system and had almost doubled through investments.

He maintained that the case could not be characterised as one involving a financial loss to the national exchequer, arguing instead that the transaction had generated profits. He also argued that the costly prosecution itself had burdened taxpayers.

Questioning the prosecution’s reliance on alleged collusion, he said the trial had concluded while several key suspects remained absent and had been declared absconders, raising questions about how the alleged conspiracy and connivance had been established.

Regarding Bushra, Barrister Safdar argued that she had no direct connection with the transaction and that neither the investigation nor the trial court’s judgment had clearly explained her specific role in the alleged offence.

He further contended that there was no evidence establishing that the money frozen in the United Kingdom represented proceeds of crime. If the funds were illicit or proceeds of crime, there could be legal consequences; otherwise, their owner was entitled to deal with the money at his discretion, he argued.

The counsel described both the reference and the charge sheet as vague, maintaining that the prosecution had failed to establish the essential ingredients of the offences against the appellants.

The court adjourned further hearings of the appeals until next week.
