articles.title: Tinubu to terrorists, bandits: Now is your chance to lay down arms
articles.summary:
• Renews surrender call 5 months after Democracy Day warning

• Vows to rescue abducted Borno schoolchildren, restore peace

• ADC accuses APC of mobilising schoolchildren for Maiduguri rally

 

From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja and Timothy Olanrewaju, Maiduguri

President Bola Tinubu yesterday renewed his call on terrorists and bandits to lay down their arms and renounce violence, declaring that his administration would not relent until peace was restored across the country.

He also assured families of abducted schoolchildren in Askira-Uba Local Government Area of Borno State that the children would be rescued.

Tinubu spoke at the All Progressives Congress (APC) North-East presidential campaign rally in Maiduguri, where he acknowledged growing concerns over persistent insecurity but expressed confidence that the country would overcome terrorism and banditry.

However, the rally drew criticism from the Borno State chapter of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), which accused the ruling party of taking schoolchildren out of their classrooms to participate in the political event, allegedly compromising their education, safety and wellbeing.

Addressing supporters at the rally, Tinubu renewed his appeal to terrorists and bandits to renounce violence, declaring: “They have the opportunity now to lay down their arms.”

Tinubu’s latest call came more than five months after he warned terrorists, bandits and kidnappers in his June 12 Democracy Day nationwide broadcast to surrender or face the full force of the Nigerian state, stressing that the window for surrender would not remain open indefinitely.

“To bandits, kidnappers, and sponsors of terror: Surrender or face the full force of the Nigerian State. These windows of surrender will not remain open forever,” he had warned.

Tinubu reiterated the warning the following day, ruling out negotiations with terrorists.

In Maiduguri, however, Tinubu neither specified a deadline for surrender nor announced any new framework for the disarmament of terrorists and bandits.

He paid tribute to officers and men of the Armed Forces, particularly those battling insurgency in the North-East, for their sacrifices in defence of the country.

“I know you are concerned about the security situation. We give respect to our men and women of the Armed Forces who are in the bush, in the sun, in the rain, who have put their lives on the line for us and for Borno, particularly Maiduguri, to have peace.

“We will achieve that peace,” he declared.

On the fate of the abducted schoolchildren, Tinubu expressed confidence that ongoing intelligence-driven operations would secure their freedom, assuring the people that children held in captivity by terrorists would be rescued.

“We will rescue them. We will rescue them, Insha Allah,” he assured.

Drawing on the historical affinity between the Yoruba of the South-West and the Kanuri of Borno, Tinubu described his campaign visit to Maiduguri as a homecoming, acknowledging the contributions of the people and political leaders of the state to his political journey and the emergence of the APC.

“I feel I have come home for a family reunion,” he said, adding: “Without the support of Borno people, we wouldn’t have gotten this far.”

He particularly acknowledged former Borno State governor, Ali Modu Sheriff, and other political leaders for their contributions to the alliances that culminated in the formation of the APC, recalling Tuesday’s presentation of a book by Sam Omatseye chronicling the evolution of political parties from the Alliance for Democracy (AD) to the APC.

Tinubu also acknowledged the contributions of Vice President Kashim Shettima to his administration and urged political leaders in the region to sustain their collaboration towards restoring normalcy, accelerating development and improving the welfare of residents.

Soliciting support for his re-election on January 16, 2027, Tinubu urged eligible voters to obtain their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and mobilise support for the APC across all elective positions, assuring the people that their loyalty and solidarity would not be forgotten.

“The love that you have shown me, the respect, the honour, will not be forgotten,” he said.

Shettima, who also addressed the rally, canvassed support for Tinubu’s re-election, citing the establishment of tertiary institutions and a Federal Orthopaedic Hospital among the administration’s interventions in Borno and other parts of the North-East.

Taking a swipe at former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, whom he described as Tinubu’s greatest challenger in the presidential race, Shettima dismissed his capacity to turn around the fortunes of Nigeria and address the developmental challenges confronting the North-East.

Drawing an analogy to underscore his position, Shettima recalled telling the people about four years ago that “cooking horn and adding salt to make it soft won’t make it eatable like meat.”

Governor Babagana Zulum commended Tinubu for the execution of development projects across the region, assuring him that the people would reciprocate his administration’s interventions at the polls.

The governor, however, appealed to the President to facilitate the resumption of oil exploration in the Lake Chad Basin and at the Kolmani oil prospecting site, as well as the development of a railway network connecting states in the North-East.

Earlier, Tinubu inaugurated the Maiduguri International Conference Centre and a two-storey National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) female corps members’ lodge, both executed by the Zulum administration.

The President commended the governor for his reconstruction and development efforts, particularly his investments in education, healthcare and infrastructure, which he said were restoring hope and delivering economic benefits to communities battered by years of insurgency.

He noted that the frequent inauguration of completed projects in Borno reflected economic progress in critical sectors directly affecting the livelihoods of residents.

“You are bringing hope back to the people. Thank you very much. We commend your efforts,” Tinubu said.

Tinubu and his wife, Oluremi, were received at the Muhammadu Buhari International Airport, Maiduguri, by Shettima and his wife, Nana; Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas; governors, members of the National Assembly and Federal Executive Council, as well as members of the APC National Working Committee, Presidential Campaign Council and City Boy Movement.

Meanwhile, the Borno State chapter of the ADC has accused the APC of mobilising schoolchildren to participate in the presidential campaign rally, describing the alleged action as a disturbing development that compromised their education and safety.

The opposition party alleged that children in school uniforms were taken out of their classrooms and mobilised to line the streets of Maiduguri in support of Tinubu and Shettima.

Director of Communications of the ADC Campaign Council in Borno, Bukar Bukar Petrol, in a statement issued in Maiduguri, said the alleged involvement of schoolchildren in partisan political activities on a school day raised questions about the ruling party’s respect for the rights and wellbeing of children.

“The African Democratic Congress (ADC), Borno State Chapter, condemns the involvement of school children in the APC presidential campaign rally in Maiduguri on an ordinary school day, Wednesday, 25 November 2026,” he declared.

Petrol questioned the rationale behind involving children in partisan political engagements at the expense of their education.

“What political message are children expected to understand or endorse when they should be in their classrooms receiving education?” he asked.

He maintained that education should remain a priority, irrespective of political considerations, stressing that children should not be withdrawn from academic activities to participate in campaign rallies.

The APC’s response to the allegations was not immediately available.

The post Tinubu to terrorists, bandits: Now is your chance to lay down arms appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: Phone tapping claim: I lied to unsettle govt –El-Rufai
articles.summary:
From Godwin Tsa, Abuja

Former Kaduna State governor, Nasir El-Rufai, has admitted that his claim that the telephone conversations of the National Security Adviser (NSA), Nuhu Ribadu, were being intercepted by opposition figures was false, telling the Federal High Court in Abuja that he deliberately made the statement as political rhetoric intended to unsettle those in government.

El-Rufai, who is in detention, made the admission yesterday while opening his defence before Justice Joyce Abdulmalik in his ongoing trial by the Department of State Services (DSS) over alleged interception of Ribadu’s telephone conversations, among other offences.

The former governor had, during an interview on Arise Television on February 13, accused Ribadu of ordering his attempted arrest, claiming that he knew about the directive because the opposition had been listening to telephone conversations of government officials.

Asked during the interview how he obtained the information, El-Rufai had replied: “He made the call because we listen to their calls.”

However, led in evidence by his counsel, Paul Erokoro, yesterday, El-Rufai admitted, after portions of the recorded interview were played in open court, that the claim was not factual but intended to create the impression that opposition figures were equally monitoring those in government.

“What I wanted to say was that the government was monitoring opposition figures and that we knew what they were doing.

“I used the word ‘tap’ as political rhetoric to make them uncomfortable. It was rhetorical, not literal. It was linguistic flourish, just to make the government uncomfortable,” he said.

Reminded by Erokoro that his interviewer had pointed out that intercepting telephone conversations without authorisation was illegal, El-Rufai said his intention was to expose the government’s alleged surveillance of opposition figures without lawful court orders.

“I was referring to the government violating the law and not someone else doing it,” he said.

The former governor explained that the word ‘we’ in the interview referred to himself and other leading opposition figures, but maintained that none of them tapped Ribadu’s phone, saying they learnt of an alleged plan to abduct and detain him through a mutual friend whose identity he declined to disclose to protect his source.

According to El-Rufai, the friend visited him after the television interview and told him that he had not actually tapped the NSA’s phone, to which he responded that he knew and had made the claim merely to unsettle the government.

He denied any involvement in phone tapping, insisting that he had neither the technical knowledge nor the equipment required to intercept telephone conversations.

Speaking on his relationship with Ribadu, El-Rufai told the court that he had known the NSA since 2003 when, as Director-General of the Bureau of Public Enterprises (BPE), he assisted him in setting up the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) by providing office accommodation and funds.

He said their relationship deteriorated when Ribadu contested the 2011 presidential election and he considered Muhammadu Buhari a better candidate, alleging that the NSA was now hostile to him because of his opposition to President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid.

Under cross-examination by prosecuting counsel, Oluwole Aladedoye (SAN), El-Rufai, who told the court that he holds a law degree from the University of London, declined to identify the opposition figures he referred to as ‘we’ during the television interview.

He also refused to disclose the identity of the person who allegedly informed him that Ribadu, Kaduna State Governor Uba Sani and the Chairman of the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) had met and agreed to ensure his arrest.

El-Rufai said he was aware of the alleged plan before his return from Cairo on February 12, adding that he resisted attempts by DSS operatives to arrest him at the airport because they failed to produce a valid arrest warrant.

He maintained that apart from the claim about tapping Ribadu’s phone, every other statement he made during the interview was factual, including his assertions that he had never stolen public funds and knew nothing about the disappearance of activist Abubakar Idris, popularly known as Dadiyata, during his tenure as governor.

He, however, admitted that the fundamental rights enforcement suits he instituted over the alleged search of his residence with a defective warrant had all been dismissed by the High Court of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) and the Federal High Court.

At the conclusion of cross-examination, Aladedoye informed the court that Erokoro had approached him before proceedings commenced to seek his assistance in facilitating the appearance of Ribadu and the ICPC chairman as defence witnesses, but that he had told him the matter was beyond his control.

Erokoro subsequently informed the court that he would file the necessary applications to secure their appearance.

Justice Joyce Abdulmalik adjourned the case until February 15 and 16 for El-Rufai to continue his defence.

articles.title: Wike asks Tinubu to assign him Imo, Kwara, says Rivers, FCT secured
articles.summary:
From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja

Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has asked President Bola Tinubu and the leadership of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council to assign him Imo and Kwara states for the 2027 presidential election, boasting that he had already put the necessary political machinery in place to deliver Rivers State and the FCT for the President.

Wike, who made the request yesterday at a Rainbow Coalition town hall meeting in Gokana Local Government Area of Rivers State, said he was prepared to take on additional political responsibilities, having concluded arrangements to secure victory for Tinubu in the two territories originally assigned to him.

“I was assigned to coordinate Rivers and the FCT. Frankly speaking, I am done with these states. All adequate political machinery have been set in motion to deliver Rivers State and the FCT for the President. So, I have not much work to do again,” he said.

The former Rivers State governor appealed to Tinubu and the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Abdul’aziz Abubakar Yari, to expand his assignment, citing reported political challenges in Imo and divisions within the political establishment in Kwara.

“As I am going now, I will plead with the DG and Mr President to have two more states for me to deliver.

“From what I am told, they are having some problems in Imo State. So, I will love to go there and deliver the state for Mr President.

“Secondly, I have not confirmed, but what I read on social media is that there are some divisions in Kwara. So I plead with the DG of the APC Presidential Council, Senator Yari, and Mr President to allow me take over Imo and Kwara states, because I am done with Rivers and FCT,” Wike said.

Canvassing support for Tinubu’s second-term bid, the minister described the President as a courageous leader willing to take difficult decisions in the national interest, citing the removal of fuel subsidy, increased financial allocations to state and local governments and the establishment of the Federal University of Environment in Ogoniland as justification for his re-election.

Wike urged the people of Gokana to sustain their political alliance with Tinubu, arguing that abandoning an established relationship for an uncertain alternative would not serve their interests.

He also commended political stakeholders in the area for setting aside their differences and rallying under the Rainbow Coalition, stressing that unity was critical to achieving their common political objectives.

Former Secretary to the Rivers State Government and Coordinator of the Rainbow Coalition in Gokana, Kenneth Kobani, described the town hall meeting as unprecedented, saying it brought together different segments of the community.

APC South-South National Vice Chairman, Victor Tombari Giadom, expressed confidence that the coalition would deliver up to 90 per cent of votes in Gokana for the APC in the 2027 elections.

Senator Magnus Abe also commended Wike for bringing hitherto divided political leaders together, saying the people of Gokana were united in their expectations from the coalition.

The meeting attracted political leaders, traditional rulers, religious leaders, women, youths and other stakeholders from Gokana and neighbouring communities.

articles.title: Mbah commissions projects, assures Oji-River of more development
articles.summary:
Enugu State Governor, Dr. Peter Mbah, has assured the people of Oji-River Local Government Area of sustained development, promising the completion of critical roads, improved water supply, 24-hour electricity and expanded empowerment programmes.

Mbah gave the assurance on Tuesday during the All Progressives Congress (APC) tour of Mmam River and Oji-River Central Development Centres and commissioning of several Smart Green Schools and Type 2 Primary Healthcare Centres built by his administration.

 

 

The projects inaugurated were Smart Green Schools at Umuagu and Umuome, Inyi, as well as Primary Healthcare Centres at Umuagu, Enugu-Inyi, Agbadala Achi and Amamkpunato Achi.

Addressing separate gatherings of the people at Central School, Inyi, and Achi Court after meeting with the electorate, polling unit by polling unit, Mbah appealed to them to bear with him for limiting the inauguration to a few projects, noting that even if he spent the entire remaining part of his administration commissioning projects, it would still not be enough, as they were in their thousands.

 

Enugu State Governor, Dr. Peter Mbah

 

He said the important thing was that the projects serve the needs of the people, promising to redouble his administration’s efforts.

“If we had continued on our commissioning spree, today, we probably would not have made it here today. But we only stopped at just two Smart Green Schools and three Type 2 Primary Healthcare Centres. We could have gone all the way to commission the rest of the projects, but we saw that we needed to come here to meet with you”, he said.

Mbah said his administration’s investments in education, healthcare, infrastructure, and human capital development were not by accident, but designed to transform the state’s economy and improve living standards.

 

 

At Inyi, he disclosed that, besides the Smart Green Schools, the government is robustly upgrading the Enugu State College of Health Technology, Oji-River, into a nursing college, with new classroom and hostel blocks and an improved curriculum. He also announced plans to commence the construction of a 660-megawatt coal-fired power plant, saying the project would guarantee 24-hour electricity supply and support round-the-clock economic activities.

 

 

On water supply, the governor said the Oji-River Water Scheme is being upgraded, with the installation of new pumps to enable it to produce up to 60 million litres of water daily. He stressed that host communities must enjoy adequate water supply.

Mbah further announced plans to empower 260 women in every ward with business grants, while women operating in cooperative clusters would receive agro-processing equipment and additional financial support. Petty traders and vulnerable households would equally benefit from grants, foodstuffs, and cash assistance.

 

 

On education, he said the Smart Green Schools were exposing children to modern technology, robotics, artificial intelligence, and innovation, while developing their critical thinking and problem-solving abilities.

“No longer will our children be limited by lack of modern skills. They will compete with their peers from every part of the world and, also, guarantee the sustenance of all that we are building today,” he stated.

At Achi, the governor said the critical roads requested by the people, including the Amakpunato-Amoli Road, had already been awarded and funded by his government, expressing optimism that they would be completed before the next rainy season.

“We recognise road infrastructure as essential to connecting communities, farmers, and businesses to economic opportunities. So, for us, it is not a favour. It is not also for acclaim. It is a necessary economic enabler,” he added.

Mbah also cited improvements in Enugu’s fiscal performance, saying the state had moved from 30th position nationally in the National Bureau of Statistics’ internally generated revenue (IGR) ranking before his administration to third, behind Lagos and Rivers states.

He said the Smart Schools and Type 2 Primary Healthcare Centres were designed to expand access to quality education and healthcare, adding that the health facilities would be adequately staffed and provide free services.

The governor urged residents to sustain the development gains recorded in the state, describing the ongoing transformation as irreversible. He also called for support for President Bola Tinubu and APC candidates in the 2027 general elections, noting that, besides addressing the challenges of strategic infrastructure and appointments in the South East before now, his administration would not have been able to execute the numerous landmark projects in the state without the president’s reforms, which had made more resources available to state governments.

In their remarks, the Senator representing Enugu West, Osita Ngwu; Member representing Awgu/Oji-River/Aninri Federal Constituency, Anayo Onwuegbu; and Member representing Oji-River State Constituency, Osita Eze, commended the administration’s projects and engagements in the area.

They assured that political mobilisation and public enlightenment would continue beyond the present tour and project commissioning, saying that the projects executed in Oji-River had provided tangible evidence of the administration’s interventions.

The Director-General, Enugu APC Campaign Council, Chief Charles Mbah, said the campaign train was in the area to appreciate residents’ support and seek their continued commitment ahead of the elections.

A major stakeholder in Oji-River LGA, Hilary Abaratu of GOWASK Construction Limited, reiterated that Mbah had delivered more than was expected of him in his second term, reminding the people that the governor remained their sure path to more infrastructural development, political relevance, and prosperity. He said they must not allow anyone to deceive them.

Earlier, Oji-River Local Government Chairman, Gregory Anyaegbudike, attributed the turnout at the rallies to residents’ confidence in the governor, assuring that the people would support APC candidates across the ballot.

The governor was accompanied by APC Deputy National Chairman, South, Dr. Ben Nwoye; the party’s South-East Women Leader, Dr. Oby Aji; members of the state party leadership, State Executive Council, government officials, and other stakeholders, including the Commissioner for Children, Gender Affairs and Social Development, Dame Ugochi Madueke, and the Commissioner for Human Development and Poverty Eradication, Prof. Benedette Ekwutosi Okoli.

Also on Mbah’s entourage, the Commissioner for Culture and Tourism and an indigene of Oji-River also featured prominently during the ward and polling unit consultations by the governor.

articles.title: Katsina directs traditional rulers to obtain clearance before receiving foreign visitors
articles.summary:
Katsina  State Government has directed traditional rulers across the state to obtain official clearance before receiving foreign visitors at their palaces, following the controversy surrounding allegations of sexual assault against the Emir of Daura, Umar Faruk Umar, by a Polish tourist.

The directive came barely 24 hours after the government suspended all official engagements and travels of the Emir and constituted a committee to investigate the allegations.

Commissioner for Information and Culture, Bala Salisu-Zango, announced the directive in a statement issued in Katsina yesterday, saying traditional rulers must henceforth obtain clearance from the Departments of Protocol and Cabinet/Security Matters under the Office of the Secretary to the State Government before hosting foreign nationals.

Salisu-Zango explained that the measure was aimed at strengthening security, ensuring proper coordination and promoting adherence to official protocols governing engagements between traditional institutions and foreign visitors.

He said the directive formed part of the administration’s broader strategy to strengthen security at the grassroots, stressing that documenting and vetting visits by foreign nationals would enable the government to monitor international engagements within traditional domains and address potential security concerns.

The government urged traditional rulers to comply with the directive in the interest of security and effective coordination of official engagements.

The development followed widespread outrage over a viral video released by a Polish tourist, Mirka Czee, who accused the Emir of Daura of sexually assaulting her during a visit to his palace on November 14, 2026.

Czee, who had undertaken a 30-day tour of Nigeria, alleged that the monarch made unwanted physical advances towards her, including touching her breasts without her consent.

The allegations generated widespread reactions on social media, with human rights advocates demanding an independent investigation and accountability.

The Daura Emirate Council had subsequently announced that it was reviewing the footage to establish its authenticity and determine whether it had been manipulated.

Spokesman for the council, Ibrahim Murtala Daura, said its official position would be communicated upon completion of the review, while an unnamed palace source reportedly denied that any inappropriate conduct occurred during the tourist’s visit.

Amnesty International Nigeria also called on the Katsina State Government and the police to conduct a transparent and independent investigation into the allegations.

The organisation subsequently condemned the reported death threats, cyberbullying and abusive messages directed at the tourist after she publicly disclosed her experience, expressing concern over attempts to intimidate her.

Following the controversy, Governor Dikko Umaru Radda on Tuesday directed the establishment of an investigative committee and suspended the monarch’s official engagements and travels pending the outcome of the investigation.

The government assured the public that the committee’s findings and recommendations would be implemented and urged residents to remain calm and law-abiding.

The Emir has yet to publicly respond to the allegations, which remain the subject of investigation.

articles.title: Pete Edochie: Tinubu, Soludo, Obi, Mbah, others mourn as iroko falls
articles.summary:
From Juliana Taiwo-Obalonye, Abuja and Obinna Odogwu, Awka

An outpouring of grief and glowing tributes has trailed the death of legendary Nollywood actor, Pete Edochie, with President Bola Tinubu, Governors Chukwuma Soludo of Anambra and Peter Mbah of Enugu, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, and prominent figures in the entertainment industry celebrating his life, exceptional artistry and enduring contributions to Nigeria’s cultural heritage.

Edochie, popularly known as ‘Ebube Dike’, died in Enugu in the early hours of Wednesday at the age of 79, drawing tributes that underscored his stature as one of Africa’s most accomplished actors and a defining figure in the evolution of Nollywood.

In a personally signed condolence message, Tinubu described Edochie as an exceptional thespian and one of the progenitors of Nollywood whose contributions to the arts and popular culture would endure for generations.

“Chief Edochie was an exceptional actor, one of the progenitors of our vibrant film industry, Nollywood. He was graceful and larger than life, both on the screen and in person.

“I recall his unforgettable portrayal of Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s evergreen novel, *Things Fall Apart*, in the 1980s, and his many brilliant performances afterwards.”

Tinubu noted that beyond acting, Edochie distinguished himself as an administrator, broadcaster and journalist whose influence on Nigerian society remained indisputable.

“As I mourn the passing of this legendary actor, I also reflect on his life. Pete Edochie lived well. He played his part and exited gracefully.

“In his works, he lives forever. Many generations will talk about the life and work of Chief Edochie in the arts industry and academia, in barbershops and marketplaces, and indeed wherever people gather.”

Tinubu extended condolences to the Edochie family, friends, associates and the entire Nigerian film industry.

Governor Soludo, who pledged a befitting state honour for the departed actor, described him as a proud son of Anambra and a cultural giant whose work carried the voice, wisdom and dignity of the Igbo to audiences across the world.

“Chief Pete Edochie was more than an actor. He was an institution, a distinguished custodian of our culture, a sage, and a source of immense pride to Ndi Anambra.

“Through his craft, he taught generations the value of dignity, courage, family and the wisdom of our elders. His passing leaves a void in our creative landscape and in the heart of our State, but his legacy will endure in the stories he told and the lives he touched,” Soludo said.

Obi extolled Edochie’s exceptional command of English and Igbo, as well as his belief in the possibility of a new Nigeria, while Mbah described him as a giant, icon and patriot, lamenting that his death coincided with the ongoing National Festival of Arts and Culture (NAFEST) in Enugu.

“Your voice may have gone silent, but your legacy will speak for generations,” Mbah said.

Minister of Art, Culture, Tourism and the Creative Economy, Hannatu Musawa, described Edochie as a national treasure and one of the finest custodians of Nigeria’s culture, language and storytelling traditions.

“This is a painful loss, not only for his family and the creative industry, but for the entire nation. An iroko has fallen.

“Chief Edochie was an outstanding actor who will not be easily replaced. He was more than an actor. He was a broadcaster, a cultural ambassador, a teacher and a father figure to generations of artists.”

Musawa noted that the late actor devoted his career to promoting African traditions, values and identity, stressing that his legacy would live on through his works and the countless young talents he inspired.-

Managing Director and Chief Executive of the Nigerian Film Corporation (NFC), Ali Nuhu, said Edochie’s commanding presence, rich proverbs and exceptional mastery of his craft gave Nigeria and Africa dignity and recognition on the global screen.

He described the deceased as an institution, a moral voice and a towering figure who represented an era of excellence, discipline and professionalism in the Nigerian film industry.

National President of the Actors Guild of Nigeria (AGN), Abubakar Yakubu, described Edochie’s death as an immeasurable loss, while actress Uche Jombo mourned the departure of one of Nollywood’s greatest pillars, whose voice and professional standards would continue to inspire generations of storytellers.

Actor Charles Inojie eulogised the deceased with traditional praise names, including “Ebube Dike,” “Ntu mara igwe” and “Okala mmadu, okala mmuo,” while media personality Adeola Fayehun, actor Artus Frank and director Glory Robinson also paid tribute.

Born on March 7, 1947, Edochie hailed from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje, in Oyi Local Government Area of Anambra State. He began his broadcasting career in 1967, rising to senior management positions before attaining national acclaim as Okonkwo in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart.

Renowned for his commanding presence, distinctive voice and masterful use of African proverbs, Edochie featured in numerous films, including *Igodo, Rituals* and *Lionheart*. He was awarded the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 and received several lifetime achievement awards.

The post Pete Edochie: Tinubu, Soludo, Obi, Mbah, others mourn as iroko falls appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: Gunmen attack NDC rally in Edo, injure one as Obi charges Nigerians to defend votes
articles.summary:
• Police launch manhunt for assailants • NDC accuses APC of masterminding attack, recalls Okpebholo’s 2025 warning

• Obi attributes secessionist agitations to bad governance • Obi, Kwankwaso take campaign to Abia tomorrow

 

From Tony Osauzo and Ighomuaye Lucky, Benin; Adesuwa Tsan, Abuja and Okey Sampson, Umuahia

The nationwide presidential campaign of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) was again marred by violence yesterday as gunmen opened fire on supporters who gathered to receive the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, in Benin City, Edo State, leaving one person with gunshot injuries and prompting the police to launch a manhunt for the fleeing assailants.

The NDC accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of orchestrating the attack, alleging that it was a fulfilment of a threat issued against Obi by Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, in July 2025.

The party also alleged that several of its supporters were injured and campaign vehicles damaged during the attack, demanding the arrest and prosecution of the perpetrators and their sponsors.

Despite the incident, Obi addressed supporters at the party’s town hall meeting, urging Nigerians to defend their votes in the 2027 general elections, promising to tackle insecurity, create jobs, fight corruption and transform the country from a consumption-driven economy to one anchored on production.

Obi, who also visited the Oba of Benin, Ewuare II, attributed secessionist agitations, including the agitation for Biafra, to bad governance, insisting that addressing Nigeria’s leadership challenges would strengthen national unity.

Meanwhile, Obi and his running mate, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, will take their campaign to Abia State tomorrow, where they are expected to engage the Aba business community on their plans for economic recovery and industrial development.

Confirming yesterday’s shooting along Airport Road, Benin City, spokesperson for the Edo State Police Command, Eno Ikoedem, said three gunmen opened fire on persons at the scene before fleeing.

“During the attack, one Aimionkhale Michael sustained gunshot injuries to his thighs and was immediately rushed to the hospital, where he is currently receiving medical attention,” the statement said.

Ikoedem disclosed that Commissioner of Police, Patrick Daaor, visited the scene and subsequently proceeded to the hospital to assess the condition of the victim.

The commissioner deployed additional personnel to secure the rally and the hospital to forestall further attacks, while operatives were mobilised to apprehend the fleeing gunmen.

“The Commissioner of Police has directed the Deputy Commissioner of Police in charge of the State Criminal Investigation Department, who is working with eyewitnesses, to ensure a thorough investigation into the incident and bring all those found culpable to justice.”

The command condemned the attack and warned individuals and groups against acts capable of threatening public safety or disrupting the peace of the state, particularly as political activities intensify ahead of the general elections.

Addressing a press conference in Abuja, the National Chairman of the NDC accused the APC of orchestrating the attack on Obi, recalling that Okpebholo had in July 2025 issued a warning concerning the former Anambra State governor’s visit to Edo State.

“On July 18, 2025, Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, publicly warned Peter Obi against entering Edo State, stating that Obi’s safety would not be guaranteed,” he said.

The chairman alleged that yesterday’s incident was an actualisation of the governor’s earlier warning, despite what he described as necessary communication ahead of Obi’s visit.

“Today, in spite of all legitimate communication, our presidential candidate, Mr Peter Obi, not even for a full-swing campaign, went for town hall meeting, has been under attack from the airport since morning. Activating or actualising the threat that was made since 2025,” he alleged.

He called on Nigerians and the international community to take note of the incident, claiming that the attacks on Obi and other NDC candidates were part of a coordinated effort to frustrate the party’s participation in the 2027 elections.

The chairman maintained that the party would not be intimidated out of the electoral contest, declaring that the attacks would neither weaken its resolve nor deter its supporters from exercising their democratic rights.

Similarly, NDC National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, described the incident as part of what he alleged was a growing pattern of violence and intimidation against the party’s members, candidates and structures across the country.

“Politics is not war. No Nigerian should be attacked, shot at, or terrorised simply for supporting a political party or exercising their democratic rights.”

The NDC urged the Inspector-General of Police and other security agencies to guarantee the safety of its members and ensure that political parties could undertake lawful campaign activities without fear of intimidation or violence.

While the police confirmed one person with gunshot injuries, the party’s claim that several others were injured had yet to be independently verified.

The police have not established the identities of the attackers, their motive or whether Obi was specifically targeted. Responses from the APC and the Edo State Government to the NDC’s allegations were not contained in the reports.

Addressing supporters at the town hall meeting, Obi urged Nigerians to remain at their polling units after casting their ballots until votes were counted, stressing that vigilance was necessary to guard against electoral manipulation.

“When you vote, don’t go home. Stay there until your vote is counted. We don’t want them to rig us out.

“We don’t want what happened in 2023 to happen again. We will get it right this time because we want to build a better society,” he said.

Obi, who contested the 2023 presidential election on the platform of the Labour Party, identified national unity, security, education, job creation and the fight against corruption as priorities of his proposed administration.

“I want to assure you that the government of Obi and Kwankwaso will unite Nigeria. We will secure Nigeria, and we will give you an opportunity to be part of the government,” he said.

The former Anambra State governor pledged to promote transparency and accountability in governance, insisting that public resources must be deployed for the collective good rather than diverted for personal interests.

“We want to build a country where people will no longer steal public money. Public money must be used for public good. That is what we want to do.”

Obi also promised to improve security in schools and protect children from kidnapping and other criminal activities, while pursuing economic policies capable of expanding employment opportunities and lifting millions of Nigerians out of poverty.

“We want to remove Nigeria from consumption to production so that all of you can have jobs. We want to build a country that cares for everybody. We want to build a society where a child of nobody can be somebody.”

He criticised President Bola Tinubu’s economic policies, alleging that they had impoverished Nigerians.

“Tinubu has put everybody into poverty. This poverty must not continue,” he declared.

Earlier, at the palace of the Oba of Benin, Obi linked secessionist agitations and calls for the disintegration of Nigeria to leadership failures and the inability of successive governments to address the needs of citizens.

Obi, who led members of the NDC Presidential Campaign Council to the palace, spoke in response to questions from the monarch and his chiefs on the state of the nation, his vision for Nigeria and the agitation by the Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB).

He maintained that the 2027 election presented Nigerians with an opportunity to enthrone competent leadership, restore security and build a country that works for citizens, irrespective of their religious, ethnic or economic backgrounds.

“Rabiu Kwankwaso and I want a united Nigeria. Talking about Nigeria, we are not talking about any other issue. All these agitations and thoughts are issues that came up as a result of misgovernance in Nigeria.

“If Nigeria is okay, everyone will want a united Africa that serves the purpose of everybody. That is why we want to create a society where a child of nobody can be somebody, irrespective of circumstance,” he said.

Obi also challenged the Federal Government to account for the N15.8 trillion purportedly generated from the removal of petrol subsidy, alleging that increased government revenues and borrowings had not translated into corresponding improvements in healthcare, education and security.

The Federal Government had, however, in August explained that subsidy removal generated N15.8 trillion in additional resources for the federation between June 2023 and December 2025, of which N5.4 trillion accrued to the Federal Government, while N10.4 trillion was distributed among states and local governments.

Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, had explained that the savings were distributed through the Federation Account rather than retained exclusively by the Federal Government.

Recalling that he undertook his National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) programme in Benin City and that his wife attended school in Edo State, Obi stressed the need to build a country where citizens enjoyed equal opportunities to succeed.

Welcoming Obi and members of his campaign council, Oba Ewuare II expressed support for the vision of a better Nigeria and offered prayers for the campaign team.

The monarch, however, said the various statistics presented by Obi during the visit would be subjected to verification by the palace.

Ahead of tomorrow’s campaign visit to Abia State, Coordinator of the NDC Presidential Campaign Council in the state and the party’s senatorial candidate for Abia Central, Nkechi Nwaogu, said Obi and Kwankwaso would engage members of the Aba business community on their plans to revitalise manufacturing, trade and commerce.

Addressing journalists in Aba, Nwaogu described Obi’s forthcoming visit to the commercial city as a homecoming, given his longstanding association with the area.

“Our brothers and sisters in Aba, the business heartbeat of Nigeria, will have the opportunity to sit, eat, and discuss with Peter Obi.

“He will listen to traders, manufacturers, shoemakers, tailors, and youths. He wants to hear how we can rebuild Aba, rebuild trade and make business work again.

“Nigeria is tired, Abia is tired, our youths have no jobs, our businesses are suffering, our naira has no value, our roads are bad, our hospitals are empty and our schools are struggling,” she said.

Nwaogu maintained that Obi was coming to Abia not merely to solicit votes but to present his economic blueprint, which also prioritises education, healthcare, security and employment generation.

She urged security agencies and the Abia State Government to provide the necessary support for a peaceful visit.

Yesterday’s shooting in Benin was the latest in a series of security incidents recorded during the NDC’s nationwide campaign.

It came barely two days after the deadly attack on the campaign of former Deputy President of the Senate, Ovie Omo-Agege, at Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, which claimed six lives, according to the police.

The NDC had on Tuesday boycotted a security meeting convened by the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, citing attacks on its members and alleged failure by security agencies to adequately protect opposition parties.

The party had also raised concerns over the withdrawal of access to an event centre booked for Obi’s town hall meeting in Benin City. The management of the facility, however, denied political interference, attributing the disagreement to a booking issue arising from a change of date.

Since late October, Obi has taken his campaign to several states, including Kogi, Nasarawa, Ebonyi, Enugu, Bayelsa, Imo, Cross River, Plateau, Benue, Lagos and Anambra, adopting town hall meetings, market tours and interactive sessions with traditional rulers, business leaders and religious organisations.

His November 4 visit to Calabar, Cross River State, was marred by a reported attack on his convoy, while suspected political thugs attacked NDC supporters ahead of a town hall meeting in Oregun, Ikeja, Lagos, on November 12, drawing condemnation from both Obi and the APC.

Last Friday, November 20, Obi addressed supporters in Onitsha, Anambra State, where he pledged that his administration, if elected, would generate, transmit and distribute at least 10,000 megawatts of electricity, alongside investments in healthcare, education and other critical sectors.

Tomorrow’s engagement in Aba, one of Nigeria’s foremost centres of indigenous manufacturing, is expected to focus on the challenges confronting entrepreneurs and Obi’s production-oriented economic agenda ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential election.

The post Gunmen attack NDC rally in Edo, injure one as Obi charges Nigerians to defend votes appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: LG autonomy: FG in limbo as APC admits constitutional friction
articles.summary:
Strengthen the independence of State Independent Electoral Commissions (SIECs) to ensure credible local government elections free from interference by state executives.

The party’s account contrasts with the position of organised labour and civil society organisations, which disclosed in September that no local government council was receiving its allocation directly from the Federation Account, while governors continued to exercise considerable influence over council finances, leadership and operations.

The Supreme Court, in its July 11, 2024 judgment in a suit instituted by the Federal Government against the 36 states, ordered that allocations standing to the credit of local governments in the Federation Account be paid directly to democratically elected councils.

The apex court also declared unconstitutional the retention and expenditure of council funds by state governments, as well as the administration of local governments by unelected caretaker committees.

Tinubu, who authorised the institution of the suit, had subsequently threatened to issue an executive order to enforce compliance following persistent delays in implementing the judgment.

An analysis of Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) reports showed that N10.48 trillion was allocated to local government councils between July 2024 and June 2026, despite the failure to achieve full implementation of the judgment.

Efforts to operationalise direct payments had seen the Accountant-General of the Federation and the Attorney-General of the Federation engage in consultations, while the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) commenced the profiling of council chairmen and authorised account signatories in early 2025.

Implementation, however, suffered further delays amid reported pressure from state governors.

While some states have enacted legislation retaining elements of the joint account arrangement, others have claimed varying degrees of compliance with the judgment.

In Anambra State, legislation enacted in 2024 retained a joint account arrangement and provided for councils to remit a portion of their allocations to the state. The Delta State Government, on the other hand, maintained that it had complied with the judgment by releasing arrears and monthly allocations directly to its 25 councils.

Legal commentators have noted that although the Supreme Court ordered direct payment of federal allocations to local governments, the judgment did not expunge Section 162(6) from the Constitution or remove other constitutional provisions empowering state legislatures to make laws governing local government administration and finances.

In its manifesto, the APC pledged to address outstanding implementation challenges, publish allocations to each of the 774 councils, establish performance and accountability standards and pursue legislative adoption of the recommendations of the revenue allocation review.

It also promised to continue constitutional and fiscal reforms aimed at devolving appropriate powers and resources to state and local governments.

Any proposed amendment to Section 162 would, however, require the approval of at least two-thirds of the members of each chamber of the National Assembly and resolutions by at least 24 of the 36 State Houses of Assembly.

While supporters of the administration have credited the Federal Government with instituting the suit that culminated in the landmark judgment, organised labour and civil society groups have continued to demand its full implementation, insisting that financial autonomy cannot be achieved while state governments retain control over council allocations.

articles.title: Fury vs Joshua fight to go ahead despite objections
articles.summary:
Councillors have approved plans allowing December’s highly anticipated Tyson Fury v Anthony Joshua fight in Cardiff to finish in the early hours.

Fans in hospitality boxes at the Principality Stadium will be allowed to drink alcohol until 03:00, with the venue closing at 03:30, to align with prime time viewing in the US.

Members of Cardiff Council’s Licensing Sub Committee were told 130 police officers would help maintain order at the event on 11 December, with twice the number of stewards present compared to a regular sports event.

A handful of residents had objected to the proposed late finish, raising concerns over noise, antisocial behaviour and public safety, but none came to the meeting.

Councillors were told the event was a “big deal for the city” and would boost the Welsh capital, in terms of “revenue” and “profile.”

Huw Thomas, chief inspector with South Wales Police, said the challenge for officers was the length of the programme, compared with other events in the stadium, saying the fight was being viewed by the force as a “three-day event”.

At Wednesday’s council meeting, it was said that 450 out of the 1600 stewards present on the night would be dedicated to fans seated on the pitch area of the stadium.

Mark Williams, Stadium Director at the Principality Stadium, said the ring walk would take place at 01:00 GMT on 12 December, with the fight expected to start at 01:30.

Regarding tickets, he said there were still tickets available, but they were “expecting a capacity of 77,000, if everything sells”.

Councillors heard objectors had raised “legitimate concerns”, but measures had been put in place to mitigate them.

Plans for more trains in the early hours of Saturday were outlined to support spectators getting home after the fight.

In response to concerns over noise, the meeting was told “no external PA system would be used”, and noise would be “monitored” on the night.

Councillors heard initial plans to have live music before the fight would not happen, but national anthems would be sung.

Regarding alcohol, councillors were told the application was for a “modest two-hour extension on the licence for one night only” and that approximately 10-15 venues were planning to open after hours for fans.

articles.title: 2026 budget: Atiku, Makinde tackle Tinubu over N10.78trn oil revenue shortfall, N31.4trn fiscal deficit
articles.summary:
From Ndubuisi Orji, Abuja

Presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, and his Allied Peoples Movement (APM) counterpart, Seyi Makinde, have raised concerns over the Federal Government’s management of the 2026 budget, demanding explanations from President Bola Tinubu over a N10.78 trillion oil revenue shortfall, the retention of a N31.4 trillion fiscal deficit and a N29.2 trillion borrowing plan despite a proposed N3.14 trillion expenditure cut.

While Atiku demanded a comprehensive account of crude oil production, sales, deductions and remittances to the Federation Account, Makinde’s campaign organisation questioned the rationale for retaining the original deficit and borrowing projections despite the proposed reduction in expenditure.

The opposition candidates also expressed concern over the implications of the government’s fiscal performance for capital project execution, infrastructure development and the living conditions of Nigerians.

Atiku, in a statement issued by the Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council (PCC), Phrank Shaibu, said Nigerians deserved a detailed explanation of the circumstances that led to the huge shortfall in projected oil revenue in the first half of 2026.

The former Vice President, citing a report by the Budget Office of the Federation, said gross oil revenue declined by N1.44 trillion in the first half of 2026 compared with the corresponding period of 2025, despite a sharp rise in international crude oil prices in the second quarter.

“The government collected N7.88 trillion against a half-year target of N18.65 trillion, even as international crude prices rose sharply in the second quarter. Tinubu cannot ask Nigerians to pay more for fuel and then wave away a N10.78 trillion gap in the oil revenue his government expected to collect.

“Tinubu made life expensive. Petrol prices drive up transport fares, diesel raises the cost of producing food and other goods, and families pay more at every turn. Now his own Budget Office shows that the government is failing to collect the oil revenue it budgeted for. Nigerians are being squeezed from both sides: they pay more, while the government delivers less.”

Atiku noted that the Budget Office had identified production constraints, weak oil sales receipts and deductions among the factors responsible for the revenue shortfall.

Consequently, Atiku challenged the administration to publish comprehensive figures on crude oil production, liftings, sales, deductions and remittances, as well as outline measures to address crude oil theft, pipeline insecurity and inadequate investment in the petroleum sector.

“Every missing naira from the budget is money that cannot support a school, equip a hospital or repair a road. President Tinubu owes Nigerians an explanation that follows the barrel from the oilfield to the public account,” he stated.

The ADC presidential candidate said his proposed administration would prioritise transparency in oil revenue management and introduce targeted measures to reduce the burden of high fuel costs on households and businesses.

“Our promise is clear: Make Nigeria Affordable Again. We will pursue accountable oil revenue and targeted relief from the cost of domestically refined fuel, so that the benefit reaches households, farmers, transporters and businesses. Subsidy follows the barrel,” he said.

Similarly, the Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) has challenged Tinubu to explain why the proposed N3.14 trillion reduction in the 2026 budget expenditure was not accompanied by a corresponding reduction in the N31.4 trillion fiscal deficit and N29.2 trillion borrowing plan.

In a statement by its Director of Strategic Communication, Richard Ihediwa, the campaign organisation described the proposed expenditure cut as insignificant when compared with alleged widespread budget padding, duplication of projects and allocation of billions of naira to non-existent projects.

Tinubu had, in a letter to the National Assembly, sought legislative approval for the repeal and re-enactment of the 2026 Appropriation Act and revision of the fiscal framework, including a reduction in expenditure by about N3.14 trillion.

The President explained that the proposed revision was intended to align the budget with existing obligations and available resources, regularise expenditures incurred by the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) on behalf of the federation and address under-provided debt service obligations, among other commitments.

However, the MDPCO questioned the rationale for retaining the original deficit and borrowing projections despite the proposed expenditure reduction.

“Our Campaign Organization therefore demands that President Tinubu should as a matter of urgency, explain to Nigerians why he retained the original N31.4 trillion fiscal deficit and N29.2 trillion borrowing plan in the budget even after the expenditure reduction,” it stated.

The campaign organisation also accused the administration of undermining fiscal transparency through the concurrent implementation of the 2024, 2025 and 2026 budgets, alleging that the arrangement created loopholes for corruption and mismanagement of public resources.

“The MDPCO contends that muddling up the national budget with the running of the 2024, 2025, and 2026 national budgets concurrently is not accidental, but apparently a deliberate tactic by officials of the APC-led administration to complicate expenditure and payment management, thereby creating loopholes for large-scale looting.

“In other climes, President Tinubu should have honourably resigned from office for this abnormality and breach of the Appropriation Act and provisions of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (as amended), which he swore to uphold, observe and protect,” it alleged.

The organisation further questioned the utilisation of borrowed funds, alleging that despite substantial borrowings, no funds had been released for the implementation of the 2026 capital budget, leaving capital project execution dependent on the 30 per cent carryover from the 2025 budget.

“The implementation of 2024/2025 budget provisions in 2026 explains the current stagnation in capital project execution,” it stated, warning that the development could worsen economic hardship and deepen the country’s infrastructure deficit.

The MDPCO advocated strict adherence to the annual budget cycle, saying Makinde would prioritise fiscal discipline, expenditure transparency and accountability under his proposed Reset Nigeria Agenda.

“Under the Makinde Reset Nigeria Agenda, the income and expenditure profiles of the national budget will be open while redirecting expenditure from the current duplication, persistent loss and white elephant projects to need-driven priorities,” it stated.

The campaign organisation maintained that effective management of public resources was critical to increasing productivity, generating employment, improving infrastructure and raising living standards.

Neither of the campaign statements contained a fresh response from the Federal Government to the specific allegations.

articles.title: Loud explosions rock Riyadh as Houthis attack Saudi ports
articles.summary:
Loud explosions rock Riyadh as Houthis attack Saudi ports

Submitted by
MEE staff
on
Wed, 11/25/2026 - 21:13

Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman expected to travel to the US next month for G-20 in first trip since start of war

This aerial photograph shows a view of the Riyadh skyline on 23 November 2026

Off

Fresh explosions rocked Riyadh on Wednesday as Yemen's Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea ports of Jeddah and Jazan, as the kingdom’s deterrence and defensive capabilities continue to be challenged.

The Houthis said that both strikes on the ports “resulted in damage” while the Saudi-led coalition acknowledged that a projectile hit the port of Jazan, resulting in minor damage and no casualties.

The port strikes followed an attack on Ras Tanura, Saudi Arabia’s largest refinery. Argus Media, which covers commodity markets, said the Houthis landed two successful blows on the facility, one at the refinery and one at the export terminal. The Houthis say they bombed Ras Tanura as retaliation for the Saudi attack on the port of Hodeidah controlled by the group.

Saudi Arabia is shooting down the majority of Houthi missiles and drones fired at it, Arab and Western officials tell Middle East Eye, but it has failed to protect key assets like energy facilities, financial centres and airports.

Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has tried to rally the US and regional states to his side. Egypt, Pakistan, Turkey and Syria have all sent or committed to delivering military support to Saudi Arabia, but with the exception of Syria - which has sent drone operators - the assistance is defensive.

The Crown Prince met US Central Command chief admiral Brad Cooper, the commander of forces in the Middle East, last week. MEE first reported the planned meeting, which was the third since fighting with the Houthis resumed in July.

The US, Saudi Arabia's top military supplier, however has not publicly committed additional support to the kingdom, although it has troops and advisers inside the country.

Iran tensions simmer

Semafor reported on Wednesday that Mohammed bin Salman will travel to the US next month for the G-20 summit in Miami. Diplomats have speculated for months whether the de facto leader of Saudi Arabia would leave the kingdom amid Houthi strikes and the chances of a new US-Israeli attack on Iran.

'Turn on the weapons spigot': Saudi Arabia asks partners for gear to deter Houthis

Read More »

Tensions between the US and Iran have been simmering for months, with the two sides exchanging blows in the Strait of Hormuz and at some land targets. The US has conducted strikes on Iran’s mainland while Tehran has responded with attacks on US military sites in Kuwait and Bahrain.

Iran said on Wednesday that an oil tanker hit a naval mine and caught fire in a "restricted zone" in the Strait of Hormuz, according to the semi-official Fars news agency.

Brent, the international oil benchmark, was up 2.5 percent on Wednesday, trading at $84 per barrel.

The Trump administration says that it is not interested in resuming the war on Iran for now, and instead wants to use economic means to collapse the government, mainly through a blockade on Iranian ports.

Iran has been hit by debilitating inflation, although regional officials who have traveled to the capital have reported busy restaurants and a sense of calm. Fars said on Wednesday that a substantial shipment of dollar banknotes had entered Iran from a neighbouring country.

articles.title: US ambassador to Israel undercuts Trump's announcement that aid to Israel will end this year
articles.summary:
US ambassador to Israel undercuts Trump's announcement that aid to Israel will end this year

Submitted by
MEE staff
on
Wed, 11/25/2026 - 18:44

The president's abrupt announcement came on the morning of the midterm elections earlier this month

Students carry placards depicting US President Donald Trump and Israel's caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu carrying guns, as they march during a general strike over rising living costs and military spending called by the CGIL trade union, in Milan, Italy, on 20 November 2026 (Claudia Greco/Reuters)

Off

US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee has undercut US President Donald Trump's assertion earlier this month that he "won't be paying Israel" by the end of this year.

Huckabee, the former governor of Arkansas who is an evangelical pastor and a staunch Zionist - by his own description - said on Tuesday at a conference in Tel Aviv that he's "not certain that there will be a cessation on an abrupt basis by the end of this year". 

That's because Washington currently gives Israel $3.8bn a year, in a 10-year memorandum of understanding that runs from 2019 to 2028.

The package also includes $3.3bn in foreign military financing and $500m in cooperative missile defence programmes.

In May, the Israeli defence ministry said that the two sides had begun formal talks to replace the current memorandum, with discussions focusing on joint investment in research, development and weapons production.

The suggested framework was to move the relationship from aid to a more reciprocal partnership. 

The Congressional Research Service, a non-partisan research body that advises the US Congress, further confirmed this in a June report that US and Israeli officials were discussing a possible shift after 2028 away from direct military aid and towards joint programmes.

Israel, a full-scale partner

In July, the Republican-controlled House of Representatives narrowly passed a $1.5 trillion budget for the US Department of War, and the bill included a controversial provision that would permanently integrate US and Israeli military tech advancements in a way that would - as Netanyahu put it - turn Israel from a foreign aid recipient to a full-scale partner. 

Future presidents would not be able to simply withdraw from such a project. 

Kushner says Israel is becoming a 'pariah' as his Board of Peace plans stall

Read More »

The National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) is must-pass legislation, as it is needed to fund all of the Pentagon's operations in the year to come. The Senate will have to consider it soon.

But emboldened by the incoming Democratic majority in January, a dozen Democrats, led by Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen, are seeking to remove the provisions related to Section 219, which establishes the "United States–Israel Defense Technology Cooperation Initiative".

The project would identify jointly developed or Israeli-origin technologies for potential integration into US systems; ensure collaborative research initiatives involving government, private sector and academic institutions in both countries protect "sensitive technology"; and ultimately align military efforts with the Department of War that include the Irregular Warfare Technical Support Directorate, the Defense Innovation Unit, the Missile Defense Agency and the United States Space Command, among others. 

Huckabee said at the Institute for National Security Studies conference on Tuesday that American lives are saved "every day" because "we pick up intelligence from our partners in Israel". 

Military ties continue

On 3 November, Trump said that his administration will not give its yearly military aid to Israel starting next year, because of a prior understanding he made with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. 

Trump added that weapon sales and other forms of military cooperation would continue. 

Speaking on Fox News, the president said that the two had agreed months ago to end the military aid since Israel no longer needed it.

Britain must stand firm against Nusseibeh's UN candidacy

Read More »

“Now, as far as paying Israel, Bibi Netanyahu and I have made a deal that we give Israel $4bn a year, and we made a deal months ago that we're stopping,” Trump said.

“We've already agreed that by the end of this year we won't be paying Israel. Now we'll help Israel if they need it,” he added.

Trump said Israel would be able to purchase weapons from the United States and other countries, suggesting that the change would affect the form of assistance rather than bring an end to military ties.

"They can buy whatever they want. They can buy whatever they want. So can Europe. We make the greatest weapons in the world," he said.

The comments came as Republican lawmakers and establishment Democrats running for Congress - as well as hundreds of statewide races - faced growing electoral pressure over support for Israel ahead of the midterm elections.

And indeed, the so-called blue tsunami, led by an energised progressive Democratic movement that wants to curb US aid to Israel, washed over Capitol Hill and state legislatures, including several governorships.

articles.title: The gold-filled mountains of Chad that hold the key to Libya's crisis and Sudan's war
articles.summary:

Submitted by
